Our diverse product offerings currently about 52 and we plan to launch additional funds in the coming quarters to further expand our passive investment options.

items.statement: Quarterly Revenue from Operations ₹445 crores vs ₹342 crores, up 30% YoY; Operating Profit ₹262 crores vs ₹184 crores, up 42% YoY
items.quote: Our quarterly Revenue from O perations was at ₹445 crores v/s ₹342 crores in Q3 FY24, up 30% year-on-year. Our quarterly Operating Profit also has shown a significant improvement in the current quarter to ₹262 crores from ₹184 crores in Q3 FY24; up by 42% YoY

items.statement: 9M Revenue from Operations ₹1,256 crores vs ₹988 crores, up 27% YoY; 9M Operating Profit ₹710 crores vs ₹528 crores, up 35% YoY
items.quote: For the nine month period, our Revenue from Operations was about ₹1,256 crores v/s ₹988 crores for 9M FY24, up by 27% year-on-year. For the same nine month period, our Operating Profit was about ₹ 710 crores v/s ₹528 crores again for nine month FY24, up by 35% year-on-year.

items.statement: Mutual fund yield improved due to TER increase on some debt schemes, mark-to-market effects, and realignment of marketing/distribution expenses
items.quote: One is that on a few debt schemes, we have increased T ER that has resulted in the increase in the yield. The other one is the mark-to-market, because of the lower AUM we are able charge some higher TER and there some yield has been improved. The third reason is on account of marketing and distribution expenses have been realigned based on the current market

items.statement: Equity yield 70-71bps, Debt 25bps, Liquid 13bps, ETF 7-8bps for the quarter
items.quote: The yield for this quarter on the equity side is in the range of around 70-71bps. Debt is 25bps, Liquid is 13bps and ETF is around 7 to 8 bps.

items.statement: Debt TER increase contributed ~1bp to overall yield improvement
items.quote: Overall, it is around one basis point.

items.statement: Equity TER to remain same; fixed income yield may see marginal improvement as rates stabilize; hybrid fund push to boost revenue contribution
items.quote: marginal improvement on the yield given the fact that as the interest rate gets stabilized and then starts coming down, we will have to give some kind of room for growth in the duration assets wherein the expenses are generally higher than the liquid fund or liquid plus fund. So, to the extent , one can expect that segment to improve. And third is, we are also pushing very aggressively our hybrid

items.statement: ESOP expense for quarter ~₹28 lakhs; non-MF revenue ₹34-35 crores
items.quote: The ESOP expense for the quarter is around ₹28 lakhs and the non-MF revenue is in the range of around ₹34 - ₹35 crores.

items.statement: Alternate business team largely in place; only senior hire planned to head alternate vertical; leveraging existing distribution for alternate growth
items.quote: to add to that Prayesh, see the cost has more or less remained the same, whatever team we have add, we have already done that except we will only do the replacement of people who Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Limited Tuesday, 28th January 2025 left. So that means incremental cost as far as people are concerned, main ly is investment function and that we are already full, so that is unlikely. There is

items.quote: As far as in the month of January is concerned, I think broadly the trend remains the same. We have not seen any significant change in the trend that you have witnessed in the previous quarter. I think we are seeing a net sales improvement for us is coming in gradually in some of the schemes already identified as there are schemes to be pushed from a broader perspective where we are seeing some bi

items.statement: SIP registration trend stable; high-ticket SIPs reduced in volatility; retail SIP focus on new customers and registrations continues; Dec cancellation rate 55-60% vs normal 50-55%
items.quote: Broadly in SIP the trend remains the same, in terms of registration numbers except we saw, especially in the lumpsum ticket SIPs. As mentioned about normally during a market volatile period, lumpsum is the one that generally gets stopped and then they again come back, which I call high-ticket SIPs. We saw some reduction in that. Therefore, we saw overall numbers marginally lower than the previous

items.quote: I think it is generally spread across all channels Lalit, mainly the IFA contribution on an incremental basis is improving, ND channel, which is the second largest channel for us. So, their contribution is improving. Infact when we did that the Conglomerate Fund, we did have participation in our funds coming from also about 22,000 IFAs contributing to the Conglomerate Fund, which also helped us in

items.statement: Unique customer base ~75 lakhs vs industry 5.26 crores; focus on new customer acquisition via ₹100-250 SIPs
items.quote: We still have only about 5.5 crore unique customer base. We have about 75 lakhs unique customer base. So given the fact that unique customer base can continue to rise, these numbers should not ultimately lead to any different kind of output except the ratio could change given the current market volatility if it sustains for say 1 or 2 quarters as we move forward.

items.statement: Large-cap, flexi-cap, balanced advantage, multi-asset allocation funds now on organized channel recommendation lists; online channel success with core funds including frontline equity, flexi cap, multi-asset, balanced advantage
items.quote: in most places. I nfact I must mention that our large-cap funds, front-end equity, and flexi-cap funds, both of them are now coming as part of the recommendation list on the organized channels. We are seeing progress in the current quarter. Even o ur balanced advantage funds, which has again been improving on overall performance, we are seeing being recommended in the organized channel. items.quote: already taken approval, w e didn’t launch of the fund which is the innovation fund, we have taken approval, we gave a preference to the Conglomerate fund over the innovation fund and then when we feel it is right, either in the current quarter or in the subsequent quarter next year, we will have this product launched. Otherwise, we have a series of product pipelines on passive side, both on passiv

items.statement: India GDP growth estimated at 6.5% for 2025; global growth 3-3.2%; RBI managing inflation; volatility expected to subside in Q1 CY2025
items.quote: India is expected to maintain its position as one of the fastest -growing major economies, with a GDP growth for 2025 estimated at about 6.5% and India's economic outlook remains though its positive, supported by strong domestic fundamentals and favorable government policies, they might also participate in the recent volatility of the international global market. Inflation is also showing signs of

items.statement: Health and life insurance new premium grew 47% YoY in Q3; health near 60% growth, term grew well, savings slower than expected, motor and two-wheeler recovered
items.quote: our health and life insurance business, which are, as I always say, the bulk of our long term value, witnessed a combined growth of 47% year on year in new premium for Q3. In this health is just shy of 60%.

items.statement: Total insurance premium ₹6,135 Cr, up 44% YoY; core insurance premium grew 42%, core insurance revenue grew 45%
items.quote: Our total insurance premium for the quarter was ₹6,135 Cr, up 44% YoY . Core insurance premium grew 42% in Q3, with the core insurance revenue growing, 45%.

items.statement: Trail revenue ARR reached ₹665 Cr, up from ₹454 Cr last year and ₹287 Cr two years ago, more than doubling every two years
items.quote: Our trail revenue is now at an ARR of ₹665 Cr, up from ₹454 Cr last year. And just to complete that story, this same number was 287 Cr exactly 2 years ago.

items.statement: Revenue grew 48% to ₹1,292 Cr, PAT grew 92% to ₹72 Cr; phase of premium growth exceeding revenue growth is behind us
items.quote: So, the revenue has grown at 48% to ₹1,292 Cr, and the PAT grew 92% to ₹72 Cr.

items.statement: Credit business down 20% YoY and 13% QoQ; secured disbursals now 1.4x unsecured at ₹2,570 Cr for quarter, ₹24 Cr revenue; core credit remains adjusted EBITDA positive but ₹40 Cr negative delta expected this year on Paisabazaar side
items.quote: The credit business has been down. It's about 20% down YoY, and this is actually the 1 st quarter where we've seen a significant reduction compared to the previous. So, it's even on quarter and quarter. It's about 13% down.

items.statement: New initiatives revenue grew 87%, adjusted EBITDA margin improved from -13% to -7%, now at 3% positive contribution margin
items.quote: We continue to strengthen our leadership in new initiatives with the revenue growth of 87%, as I said, and adjusted EBITDA margin moving from minus 13% to minus 7%, with a 3% contribution.

items.statement: PB Partners added 20,000 advisors in Q3 to reach 270,000 advisors across 18,900 PIN codes covering 99% of India
items.quote: PB Partners continues to lead, which is our agent aggregat or platform. Today it has 270,000 advisors. Last quarter was 250,000 advisors. So, in the in the last one quarter, we've added another 20,000 advisors.

items.statement: UAE insurance premium grew 58% YoY, aligning towards health and life similar to India business
items.quote: Our UAE insurance premium has grown at 58% YoY and is now aligning more and more towards health and life similar to our India business.

items.statement: Long-term contribution margin target of 50-55% unchanged; 10% delta from current levels not out of imagination; prioritizing growth over short-term profitability
items.quote: I don't think one should rule out a much higher contribution margin than today, and I don't think a 10% delta from where we are is out of imagination in any way.

items.statement: POSP business drives new initiatives; 5% contribution margin not out of reach but no short-term guidance given due to competitive dynamics
items.quote: I think, 5% is certainly not out of reach. I hope we do better than that. Let's see how that market evolves.

items.statement: Healthcare foray: deep negotiations with investors ongoing, expect announcement in ~30 days; board authorized negotiations 45 days ago
items.quote: I was authorized by the Board about 45 days ago to have negotiations with the multiple parties in trying to get investors on board. We are in deep negotiations with the investors. We are in a position to announce something in about 30 days or so, I hope.

items.statement: Savings growth still north of 30% for quarter and January; ahead of industry but impacted by market cycles
items.quote: See when we say slow growth , do appreciate, it was still north of 30 for the quarter, and even for the month. Well, it was quite okay. And even in January we are seeing quite okay.

items.statement: Health new business at 0% margin (slight loss) but NPV positive; health renewal growth at 46%; new business outperformance creates medium-term margin pressure but good stress
items.quote: Whereas the new business is growing faster, fresh health business comes at 0% margin. And that's obvious. In fact, a little bit of loss actually. So that continues to hurt us.

items.statement: ~2/3rd to 70% of business from tier-2/3 cities; expect this share to grow; national digital/TV advertising model limits incremental cost
items.quote: I would say that today, about 2/3rd to 70% of our business comes from tier-2 & tier-3 cities. And I think this number will grow.

items.statement: Unsecured lending expected to recover to 15%+ industry growth; secured growing rapidly at ₹1,000 Cr/month; both remain focus areas
items.quote: Unsecured is one which gives you higher ROA so unsecured as an industry should get back from this base to about 15%+ growth, which the regulator also hopefully would be comfortable with.

items.statement: No new financial guidance for FY27 or beyond; previous ₹1,000 Cr net income guidance based on renewals doubling every 2 years remains unchanged
items.quote: We don't like to give guidance very often and usually we are long term thinkers, and that guidance was on some fundamental blocks of the business. Those blocks are fairly unshakable.

items.statement: Health insurance: industry new business claims ratio 25%, renewal 75%; Policybazaar brings fresh lives at reasonable loss ratios; affordability addressed via monthly policies
items.quote: On new business , claims ratio is 25 % and on renewal business as an industry, the claims ratio is 75%.

items.statement: Health distribution is 'our own race'; no focus on competitors; 5.5 lakh new customers acquired monthly via credit score product
items.quote: Customers typically exp erience credit score as a first product. So, there we continue to acquire about 5.5 lacs new customers every month. That's not down.

items.statement: POSP premium ₹1,326 Cr, Corporate premium ₹390 Cr in Q3; PB Connect revenue ₹24 Cr (up from ₹7 Cr in Q2), loss of ~₹4 Cr/quarter
items.quote: From numbers perspective, POSP is ₹1,326 Cr the premium of the quarter. Corporate is about ₹390 Cr

items.statement: Cost rationalization: vacant offices notices given, emptying by April; seat cost ₹8-10k/month; savings impact from April onwards
items.quote: We've already given the notice to the real estate Guy, that we are getting rid of those seats. So the offices will get emptied by April.

items.statement: Health renewal rates at highest ever in December on policy count basis; 1st year and 2nd year+ renewals both at peak; modular products with rising no-claim bonus improve persistency
items.quote: very happy to tell you that in December, and we look at it on a number of policies basis, because I think that's the most important number both our 1st year renewal and our second year renewal onwards are at the highest rates that we've ever had.

items.statement: Not changing strategy due to 1/n commission accounting; 3-year plans advantage for Policybazaar as not all can invest in growth
items.quote: We are not so small there like, honestly, we're not. We're not so sm all that we would change our strategy basis, some commission payout or something of that sort

items.statement: Agent productivity varies by quarter; Q3 productivity lower due to ambitious targets; Q4 expected higher productivity as no capacity addition
items.quote: I would say in Q3, it was similar that yes, productivity was not as good as we would have hoped to be. Because, like you said, we had just set very ambitious growth targets.

items.statement: Core credit business EBITDA margin 9%, contribution margin 45%; more efficient than Policybazaar core due to NPV factor
items.quote: EBITDA margin is 9% and contribution is 45%. So it's actually more efficient than Policybazaar, because there's also a factor of the N PV of Policybazaar.

items.statement: Insurance CSAT first time above 90% at 90.2%, up from last quarter
items.quote: And the insurance CSAT is now for the 1st time above 90% and 90.2% up from last quarter.

items.statement: Apparel retail demand weaker than expected due to underwhelming festive season and decreased discretionary spending; demand picked up post-December 15 and January has been fairly good YoY
items.quote: The apparel retail demand remained weaker than expected, driven by underwhelming festive season and decreased consumer spending on discretionary items.

items.statement: Target low single-digit SSSG in Q4 FY25 and mid-single-digit SSSG in FY26 with double-digit revenue growth
items.quote: Way forward, our first step is to achieve low single-digit SSSG in FY '26. Second would be grow our footprint, increasing the number of stores in our portfolio.

items.statement: Plan 80-90 net store additions in FY25 and 120-150 net additions in FY26
items.quote: Going forward, next year, we aspire to open anywhere between 120 to 150 net additions for the next year.

items.statement: Plan to phase out 10-15 more small stores in Q4 FY25; this will be the last set of small store closures
items.quote: We continue to rationalize our smaller stores and plan to phase out another additional 10 to 15 stores in Q1 this year. This will be the last set of small stores closures.

items.statement: Opened 61 net new stores in 9M FY25; target 80-90 net additions for full FY25
items.quote: In line with this approach, we opened 61 net new stores, on a net basis for the 9 months FY '25. And for the full year, we plan to do a total between 80 to 90 net additions.

items.statement: Achieved 32% EBITDA margin in 9M FY25 and 32.5% in Q3 FY25 through cost control and disciplined discounting
items.quote: Despite this, we upheld good P&L hygiene and achieved impressive EBITDA margin of 32%.

items.statement: Target pre-IndAS EBITDA margin of 18-20% in FY26 even with low single-digit SSSG
items.quote: On a steady state basis, I think we will target a pre-IndAS EBITDA of between 18% and 20%, with at least being 18% going up to 20%.

items.statement: Average selling price increased to INR769 driven by favorable product mix shift, not price hikes
items.quote: As of December, our average selling price stood at INR769, driven by favorable shift in our product mix.

items.statement: Value-added products growing; chudidaar/leggings now 35-40% of sales vs earlier higher reliance
items.quote: From a split perspective between chudidaar leggings and value-added products, I'm not having it right now. I'm guesstimating it will be, chudidaar leggings should be between 35% and 40%.

items.statement: Gross margin benefited majorly from cotton price decline; steady-state GM seen at 62-63%
items.quote: I think we've had cotton prices coming down. And I think finally we have seen the full benefit of cotton prices. So we have done a 64% GM in Q3. I think, steady state, we see a 62.5% to 63% GM on a steady-state basis.

items.statement: Inventory days at 99 as of Dec 2024; target 90-95 days for full FY25; aim to convert >50% EBITDA to operating cash flow
items.quote: For the full year, we anticipate our inventory days to stabilize between 90 and 95 days, ensuring operational efficiency and healthy working capital management, generating decent, high operating cash flows.

items.statement: Debtor days increased 6-7 days due to INR9-10 cr delayed payment from one LFS partner received in early January
items.quote: One of our LFS partners has actually paid us late. That one payment of a total of about INR9 crores to INR10 crores which was supposed to come in December, actually came in, in January, first week.

items.statement: New customer acquisition slowed; repeat customers intact; drop in bill cuts due to fewer new customers
items.quote: I think the largest issue for us is new customer acquisition has slowed down. Repeat, our repeat customers who are coming in to buy a Go Colors is very much there.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth flat for 9M FY25; North mid-single-digit positive, West low-single-digit positive, South weak due to extended rains
items.quote: Same-store sales growth remained flat, reflecting the subdued market environment as heightened inflation prompted customers to postpone discretionary apparel purchases.

items.statement: Full price sales ratio at 95.1% in challenging demand environment
items.quote: Our full price sales ratio accounted for 95.1% in a challenging demand environment.

items.statement: Added variable pay component for front-end staff linked to SSSG targets from Q1 FY26 to drive revenue growth
items.quote: We are creating a variable component, additional variable component over and above what we have, for our front-end employees with certain targets on SSSG and overall growth.

items.statement: Shifting expansion to horizontal growth in new cities/towns; 40% existing clusters, 60-65% new markets
items.quote: Maybe now it's a 40-60 Go Fashion ( approach, where 40% might come from existing clusters and 60%, 65% would come from newer markets

items.statement: First Dubai store on track to open by April 2025 through Apparel Group partnership
items.quote: I'm also pleased to share that we are on track of opening our first store in Dubai. And our stores should open by April 2025 through Apparel Group.

items.statement: Promoter pledge increased 1% in Q3 due to urgent family requirement; short-term in nature; timelines for reduction to be shared later
items.quote: We had an urgent requirement within the family. And we had to do this, unfortunately. And this also continues to remain short term in nature.

items.statement: Market share study with Technopak underway; results expected by Q4 FY25 results declaration
items.quote: We are actually doing a study with Technopak right now as we speak. We did one during the IPO, and it was long due. So in fact, the study is going on right now. And hopefully when we are declaring the Q4 results, the new study on market share, the overall market size, everything will be in place.

items.statement: EBO channel revenue grew 8.5% YoY to INR463 cr in 9M FY25; LFS stores temporarily down 80-90 due to partner renovations
items.quote: Our EBO channel revenue for 9 months FY '25 stood at INR463 crores, reflecting an 8.5% year-on-year increase.

items.statement: Mature EBO store revenue INR1.3-1.5 cr with 31-32% store-level EBITDA after rent; gross margin 68%
items.quote: A matured store would be higher; would be about maybe INR1.3 crores, INR1.4 crores. I'm not having the numbers close to me, but it will be I think in the range between INR1.3 crores and INR1.5 crores. Gross margin profile would be similar across matured and nonmatured, so gross margin would be 68%. So matured store will deliver a store-level EBITDA of about 31% to 32% after rent.

items.statement: Advertising spend kept at 1.9% of revenue in 9M FY25 due to sluggish demand
items.quote: Our advertising spends as a percentage of revenue stood at 1.9% for the 9 months. We have strategically taken a call to keep it intact because of the sluggish demand environment.

items.statement: Targets INR10,000 crores food and FMCG revenue by end of FY27
items.quote: And therefore, our target of reaching to INR10,000 crores by end of FY '27 seems to be very much achievable.

items.statement: Targets 1 million direct retail outlets by exit FY27
items.quote: We have taken a target to exit FY '27 at 1 million direct coverage.

items.statement: Expects edible oil industry volume growth of 6-7% and company growth of 8-9%
items.quote: Our expectation, to answer your question straight, the demand for the packaged edible oil should -- I mean, the industry should keep growing within the range of 6% to 7%. And our growth, of course, we feel that we should be able to grow at 8%, 9% kind of number.

items.statement: Targets food and FMCG average volume growth of 20% plus
items.quote: See, we have said earlier that food and FMCG, we wish to continue at an average growth rate of 20% plus.

items.statement: Expects food business EBITDA margins to start growing after FY28
items.quote: I think fo od will remain in the investment or a growth stage, rather, I would say, till FY '2 8. And therefore, the EBITDA margins for the food ideally should only start growing after FY '28

items.statement: Gohana integrated food facility capex of INR1,300 crores, majorly IPO funded
items.quote: This will be built with an overall capital outlay of close to INR1,300 crores, which is majorly funded through an IPO funding.

items.statement: Plans bigger capex next year for wheat flour capacity expansion
items.quote: And next year also, we plan to have bigger capex. So wheat flour, we want to be reasonably large player in this category.

items.statement: Gohana facility commenced rice and mustard oil production, first commercial dispatch in January 2025
items.quote: We have commenced the production at rice to rice and mustard oil facility and have achieved first commercial dispatch from this factory in January '25.

items.statement: Gohana integrated facility expected fully operational by end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: This integrated facility is expected to be fully operational by end of first quarter of next financial year.

items.statement: Gohana plant has 600 tons paddy per day and 500 tons rice per day capacity
items.quote: The most important part is that in Gohana, we have almost 600 tons paddy per day and 500 tons of rice per day capacity, which is very big enough for us to use it.

items.statement: Edible oil capacity utilization reasonably well placed for future growth
items.quote: The capacity utilization in this segment continues to be reasonably well placed, which is suggestive of the fact that any future growth can be accommodated easily.

items.statement: Food business capacity utilization at 53%
items.quote: As far as the food is concerned, again, we have enough capac ities in place. The utilization of capacities at 53

items.statement: Largest soya nugget producer in India at 6,000 tons per month across three plants
items.quote: So we are the largest soya nugget producers now in India at 6,000 tons per month.

items.statement: Edible oil industry volume growth subdued at low single digit for last five quarters
items.quote: In both edible oils and wheat flour industry has been showing subdued growth in low single digit for last five quarters.

items.statement: Rural demand recovery started after good monsoons from September onwards
items.quote: Only after good monsoons this here, we saw the route consumption pick up. And good consumption, good response we saw only after September.

items.statement: Urban consumption remains stretched due to inflation
items.quote: Urban stress continues, and we can see that urban consumption is stretched.

items.statement: Normalized company EBITDA range INR3,500-3,600 crores; above indicates commodity cycle gains
items.quote: our normalized EBITDA, as we are saying earlier also, is anywhere in the range of INR3,500 crores to INR3,600 crores. Anything ab ove that is suggestive of the fact that we have witnessed a commodity cycle gain in that particular quarter or period

items.statement: Edible oil normalized EBITDA per ton range INR3,750-3,800
items.quote: It would be in the range of 3,750 to 3,800, because that's how, when you look at a blended level, you get an EBITDA of 3,000 -- normalized EBITDA of 3,500 level at a company level.

items.statement: Food and FMCG segment EBITDA neutral for quarter and 9 months ended December 2024
items.quote: Overall food and FMCG business more or less remained EBITDA neutral for the quarter and the 9 months ended December '24.

items.statement: Rice inventory valuation loss of INR50 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: So the inventory loss right now sitting in this number which is, again, this time we have taken given the fact that market has corrected downward is close to INR50 crores.

items.statement: Alternate channel (MFS, e-comm, q-comm) trailing 12-month revenue exceeds INR3,000 crores
items.quote: One of the highlight of course in this entire performance in the alternate channel comprising of MFS, e-comm and q-comm that is growing faster than the general trade and now contributes, a sizable business with a trailing 12 months revenue in excess of INR3,000 crores.

items.statement: HoReCa channel contributing close to INR600 crores on trailing 12-month basis
items.quote: HoReCa channel, which we started a couple of years back, continues to grow for us and is now contributing close to INR600 crores of business basis 12 months

items.statement: Alternate channel grew 16% in Q3; e-comm 41%, quick-comm 81%
items.quote: Alternate channel continues to -- continues to be a good story for the company. This channel grew healthy 16% during the quarter in which e-com and quick-com grew by 41% and 81%.

items.statement: Palm oil prices moderated in late December but remain elevated due to 20% duty hike in September 2024
items.quote: Industry witnessed so me downward correction in the prices in the later part of December, but still prices remained higher as compared to the past quarters, primarily due to high duty imposed by the government in the month of September '24

items.statement: Expects January price levels to sustain for Q4 FY25
items.quote: But what our expectation is that the level which we have seen in the month of January will continue to play, at least for this quarter.

items.statement: Edible oil volume growth 4% led by soya, sunflower, mustard; palm volume weak due to high prices
items.quote: In edible oil business, in spite of high prices, we could register a single-digit volume growth led by soya, sun and mustard oil. This volume growth would have been in single-digit had the palm -- could have been high single-digit had palm prices remained below the soya and sun.

items.statement: Food and FMCG volume growth 23% in Q3 across all food products
items.quote: In the food and FMCG business, we delivered yet another quarter of a sizable volume growth of 23%. The growth came on the back of all the food products showing sizably.

items.statement: Direct coverage of 8.2 lakh outlets, total reach 2.1 million outlets, 40,000+ towns with population <100k
items.quote: On distribution front, we continue to work on growing it and now have a direct coverage of more than 8 lakh outlets and total reach of more than 2.1 million outlets. In terms of rural distribution expansion, we now reach more than 40,000 towns and have -- which have got a population of less than 100,000.

items.statement: Rural saliency close to 30% of overall business
items.quote: And rural saliency in our business remains at a close to 30% of our overall business.

items.statement: Edible oil market share flat, down 20 bps to 18.1%; Fortune brand share gained
items.quote: We actually dropped by 20 basis point on overall market share from 18.3% to 18.1%. But the encouraging part of this entire story on market share is that Fortune market share actually has gained.

items.statement: Wheat flour market share up from 5.3% to 5.8%; Basmati rice share down from 7.4% to 6.1%
items.quote: We have gained market share, gone up from 5.3% to 5.8% now. Basmati rice market share has come down from 7.4% to 6.1%.

items.statement: Soya nuggets: largest producer with own Wenger technology plants; sees healthy competition from Marico Saffola
items.quote: We are possibly the only people to have three locations of nugget. And as you know, these are light products. So cost of freight is very, very important, and we have that logistic advantage because we have soya bean plant in Nagpur with Vidisha.

items.statement: Government imposed 20% duty on edible oils in September 2024 to support farmers
items.quote: primarily due to high duty imposed by the government in the month of September '24.

items.statement: Duty reduction uncertain as oils trade below MSP; government priority is farmers and consumers
items.quote: On the duty, it's anybody's guess, government after a long wait increased the duty to support the Indian farmers. Unfortunately, today also these are trading way below the MSP. So I mean, you can call it 50-50, whether they can reduce the duty or not.

items.statement: Palm oil pricing driven by Indonesia/Malaysia biodiesel policies (B35/B40) and geopolitical factors
items.quote: See on the pricing, it has become a very political product, both for Indonesia and Malaysia. The biodiesel program is important and the food demand. Yes. So as you rightly mentioned, the prices actually were higher by 15% to 20% compared to the other soft oil -- now market is correcting, the spread is reducing and this biodiesel program of Indonesia, whether it is B40 or eventually, it will only r

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance INR2,800-2,900 crore with EBITDA margin 15%+ for full year

items.statement: CarWale stronger in top 25 cities for used cars above Rs 8 lakh; OLX stronger in B/C/D-class towns for used cars up to Rs 8 lakh
items.quote: CarWale has very strong strength because it's such a new car platform on cars above 8 lakhs for used cars. And OLX is strong up to eight lakhs.

items.statement: Competition in remarketing is primarily offline sales; CarTrade's phygital model with 130+ physical locations and digital marketplace creates network effects
items.quote: We are generally competing with a very offline methodology of sales. So, if a bank or an NBFC or an individual didn't sell vehicles in an auction format, digital auction format, they would sell it offline directly.

items.statement: Cost structure designed for operating leverage; minimal incremental cost with revenue growth; ESOP costs down 37% YoY to Rs 2.79 crore per quarter
items.quote: It's actually it's in a standalone. It is down by 37% to 2.79 crores a quarter.

items.statement: Monthly active unique visitors across CarWale, BikeWale, OLX India reached 79 million; >150 million annual customers (>10% of India population)
items.quote: We have achieved 79 million monthly active, unique visitors across all our three platforms.

items.statement: abSure/Signature used car franchise stores expanded to 375-400 across CarWale (180) and OLX (170-180)
items.quote: We have got an abSure/Signature outlets for CarWale, which is, I think, the 180 odd stores now. And we acquired OLX, we got another, I think about 170 -180 stores there as well.

items.statement: Revenue growth driven by higher OEM ad spend, increased traffic, and more vehicles sold via platform; not reliant on single factor
items.quote: It's actually all the above. One is the manufacturer spend more money, second is as I gave the figure a little earlier. The traffic itself is up substantially year-on-year in CarWale and BikeWale.

items.statement: Management does not provide revenue growth guidance but expresses confidence in market conditions and business positioning
items.quote: We don't give guidance Sachin around revenue growth rate, but we do feel that market conditions are reasonable and you know, all the October, December tends to be a little high in terms of the quarter for the consumer group always.

items.statement: OLX integration focused on backend tech unification while maintaining separate consumer-facing brands; first steps of common backend functions implemented this quarter
items.quote: What we tend to merge always or tend to make it easy for people to do is the backend. So, there's a dealer on OLX and CarWale, can we give them one simple tool to upload cars on both platforms, right?

items.statement: Repossession volume improvement may not be a one-quarter phenomenon but difficult to predict beyond near term
items.quote: Whether it also seems likely these are not one-quarter phenomenon, so it seems likely that it could be a there for a while. But it's hard for us to predict beyond that.

items.statement: OLX employee cost rationalization contributed to margin improvement; organization restructuring post-acquisition now largely complete
items.quote: Yes, there is some cost side rationalization because of that, absolutely on the employee side. But it takes us time because after the M&A, it takes us time to balance tech costs, employee costs, organization charts.

items.statement: Financing and transaction products on CarWale/BikeWale/OLX gaining traction; two-wheeler financing volumes scaling; OEMs adopting CarTrade tech on their own platforms
items.quote: Some have scaled, especially in two-wheelers, we find the volume is pretty high. So, these are all products for the future.

items.statement: Medium-term guidance: 25-30% revenue CAGR, $400M revenue in 3-4 years, 40% EBITDA margin
items.quote: we will be looking at a growth of anywhere between 25% to 30% on a CAGR basis, and will be a 400 million revenue company in the next 3 to 4 years, with a very significant EBITDA margin of 40%.

items.statement: DDC cartridge capacity expanding 5x from 40M to 220M units in 3-4 years; 90M expected by end of FY26
items.quote: we are going almost -- increasing our capacity 5x from the 40 odd million to almost 220 million in the next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin 36% (INR143 cr on INR393 cr revenue); 9M FY25 EBITDA INR284 cr on INR1,000+ cr revenue
items.quote: In the quarter, we delivered a revenue of INR393 crores and an EBITDA of INR143 crores. Especially a highlight on EBITDA, where our EBITDA for the quarter was actually more than the previous two quarters combined and with a very strong margin of 36%.

items.statement: GLP-1 customer forecasts revised upward multiple times; customers across major markets including Brazil, India, China; Tirzepatide customers already onboarded for NCE-1 2026 deadline
items.quote: our customers have increased the forecast upwards on multiple occasions. So which gives us confidence and that's why we are investing for this capacity.

items.statement: Biologics & DDC revenue currently mostly MSA (pre-approval); steady state mix expected 80% CSA (commercial) / 20% MSA; FY26 a cusp year for transition
items.quote: in steady state, we would have the ratio actually 80-20 in favor of CSA, which is a commercial revenue. While we reach steady state in a couple of years, we will have FY26, which is basically a cusp year where we will evolve from predominantly MSA to a significant CSA.

items.statement: Net debt INR581 cr (INR5,817M) at end Q3 FY25; target debt/EBITDA <1x medium-long term; aim to be debt-free before end FY27
items.value: INR581 cr net debt; <1x debt/EBITDA target
items.quote: we are net of deposits and net of cash and cash equivalents about INR5,817 million on our debt, which is INR581 crores to be precise. And we are anticipating a healthy over a medium to long term period debt to EBITDA of less than one. We actually aim to be debt free before end of financial year '27.

items.statement: Raised INR801 cr (INR8,010M) in Q3 FY25; half used to retire high-cost and guarantee-backed debt; balance kept for capex
items.quote: We raised about 801 crores, 8,010 million, as you would have known. And we've already used half of it to retire some of our high cost and some of our complicated guarantee backed debt.

items.statement: 20 GLP-1 customers (who's who of global generics); multiple customers per molecule; contracts include capex participation, reservation fees, 12-18 month binding forecasts
items.quote: Today, we have got 20 customers in GLP-1, and I can tell you these are who's who of the global generic space. Here also, there are multiple customers, who are our customers for more than one GLP-1.

items.statement: Isolator-based DDC capacity hard to replicate; 5-year lead time for new entrants to first revenue; significant headstart with multiple technical transfer batches
items.quote: If today someone were to come in and start putting the investment, put in an order, just to get a filling line, it will take them anywhere between 24 to 36 months. And even if they have once the machine comes in 3 years from now, to take the batches, you need to generate 6 months of data before you can go to FDA.

items.statement: DDC contracts 5-15 years (avg ~10 years); volume-based staggered pricing; some contracts include profit-share/royalty upside
items.quote: Our contracts are typically between 5 to 15 years. So you can take an average of about 10 years of all our DDC contracts, that's your first question. And in terms of pricing, obviously, as a typical CDMO, we have a volume-based staggered pricing

items.statement: FY26 quarterly fluctuations expected due to GLP-1 market formation timing (Canada Jan 2025, Jan 2026, bulk in late March); revenue recognition skewed to H2
items.quote: FY26 would kind of be a little bit ambiguous in terms of what exactly can we sell. All the 90 million that we will have before the end of the year, we would like to believe so, but can we sell the 40 million? 100%.

items.statement: Export revenue expected between $180 million to $200 million for FY25
items.quote: the exports of Sundram Fasteners, depending on how we close could be between $180 million to $200 million as a broad range, and maybe closer to $200 million.

items.statement: EBITDA trajectory expected between 17% to 18% for FY26
items.quote: taking into account the rupee weakness and additional exports volume in FY '26, our EBITDA trajectory could be between 17% to 18%.

items.statement: Export revenue expected to scale up by 15% in FY26 due to new EV orders
items.quote: That is our expectation.

items.statement: Domestic auto industry expected to grow 5-6% in FY26; export growth muted
items.quote: the domestic segment is expected to grow at about 5% to 6%, consolidated. I am talking about all the segments put together, it will be sort of a middle single digit. And as far as the export is concerned, the growth will be muted.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle production dipped 8% in H1 FY25, recovered 2 percentage points in Q3
items.quote: the commercial vehicle industry on a production front saw 8% dip compared to the last year. And it was our estimate that going forward for the second half, Q3 as well as Q4, we estimated the commercial vehicle segment to pick up 2 to 3 percentage points from the dip it was. And true to our prediction, it is now about 6%.

items.statement: Passenger car entry-level and sedan segments dropped 15-16%; SUVs now 65% of segment
items.quote: the entry level cars and the sedans have had a big drop, close to 15%, 16%. And the SUVs are dominating the segment today with 65% of the industry segment.

items.statement: Tractor demand picked up in Q3 FY25 on good kharif and rabi seasons
items.quote: with a good kharif season and now rabbi sowing season being high and also the rabbi crop expected to be good, the tractor demand has also slightly picked up in the third quarter, and the momentum is likely to continue in the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA at 16.1% vs 17% for nine months; product mix and power costs pressured margins
items.quote: On revenues of Rs. 1,256 crores, total revenue, we have had a contribution of about 26% and EBITDA at 16.1% compared to nearly 17% for the nine months' period.

items.statement: Raw material procurement rates dropped 2-3% but adverse product mix offset benefit
items.quote: raw materials have been stable, and we have experienced about 2% to 3% drop in the procurement levels. When I say procurement levels, I mean the procurement rates. But this quarter the product mix had moved slightly against us and where either the realization of the parts was lower, or the RM content were higher. And that has had an impact on the material or the gross margin.

items.statement: Power costs increased due to state tariff revisions and open access charge indexation
items.quote: all state governments now every year revise the power costs, the fixed element and also the tariff. Also, all the power which you procure under the group captive scheme get revised because the open access charges are indexed to this tariff. So, these are sort of impact.

items.statement: Wind energy capacity at 100% utilization; revenue share 5-6% targeting higher single digit
items.quote: With respect to the wind related, the capacities are in place, and we have come to the 100% utilization of the installed resources. And we have seen an uptick in the revenue, thereby pushing up our auto, non-auto ratio also moving from 60:40 to now we are looking at 65:35.

items.statement: EV orders on stream; customer schedules indicate pull from Q1 FY25 (Jan-Mar), better visibility by Q2 FY26
items.quote: the customers have indicated the schedules starting from current Q1. And I think it's on stream from our side with respect to the new product development is validation. And hopefully, by Q2 we will get better visibility in terms of pull from the customer end.

items.statement: EV order ramp-up trajectory recalibrated; earlier guidance of Rs. 200-250 crore year 1, Rs. 450-500 crore year 2 now premature
items.quote: Hazarding an estimate would be too premature now, but definitely there will have to be some recalibration to that.

items.statement: Incurred Rs. 300 crores capex in nine months FY25; new capacities for EV and wind address CY2025-26 requirements
items.quote: Our borrowings have moved up, this is because we have incurred capital expenditure of nearly Rs. 300 crores, and there has also been built up in the inventory and in anticipation of a stronger Q4.

items.statement: Existing capacity utilization at 60-65%; new capex utilization to improve from FY26
items.quote: With respect to the capacity utilization on our existing businesses, it hovers between 60% to 65%. And on the new CapExes whatever we have invested, so it also addresses the requirements of customers starting calendar year 2025 as well as 2026. So, we should be seeing better numbers of the new investment in, say, '26.

items.statement: Exports grew 15% YoY to Rs. 1,174 crores in 9M FY25; 13% growth in dollar terms
items.quote: exports have moved sharply from Rs. 1,024 crores to Rs. 1,174 crores, registering a 15% growth. And we have grown in volume terms, in dollar terms, and rupee depreciation has also helped, but significantly we have grown in dollar terms.

items.statement: Rupee depreciation benefits profitability; exports $180-200M vs minimal imports
items.quote: 100%, sir, because the exports of Sundram Fasteners, depending on how we close could be between $180 million to $200 million as a broad range, and maybe closer to $200 million. And our imports are not significant except in a year where we import for capital expenditure requirements. So, whenever there is a rupee depreciation, we tend to benefit.

items.statement: FX mark-to-market loss in Q3 on euro/GBP receivables and hedges; notional, to reverse in Q4
items.quote: the rupee had a weakness. Not only rupee weakened, but also European currencies weakened which were very strong in the previous quarter. And some of our receivables in euro and GBP were mark-to-market at much higher levels. So, they have to be reindexed. Also, the currency derivatives where we had taken some hedges again had to be done mark-to-market under the accounting standards. And all of that

items.statement: Inventory and receivables buildup in anticipation of stronger Q4 pushed up borrowings and interest cost
items.quote: there has also been built up in the inventory and in anticipation of a stronger Q4, because these are based on customer schedules and forecasts. And as you know, Q3 is traditionally a weak quarter because especially for the exports, and we have experienced that. So, the inventory buildup and the receivables have pushed up the borrowings, which is reflecting in the slightly higher interest cost.

items.statement: Top 5 customers contribute ~35% revenue; key domestic: Tata Motors, Maruti, Mahindra; key export: Cummins, GM
items.quote: the customer concentration, if you look at it, it would be in the range of 35% for the top five. And one significant portion of the customer base is, we do not have large exposure to any individual customers.

items.statement: Fastener market share 40-45% in India; competitors include Sterling Tools, Deepak Fasteners, Right Tight Fasteners
items.quote: I think we are the number one in the Indian market I think with a market share of say close to 40% to 45%, that is the market share which we would be commanding today. And we have competition in the form of either Sterling Tools or Deepak Fasteners or Right Tight Fasteners.

items.statement: Auto/non-auto revenue mix shifted from 60:40 to 65:35 due to wind energy ramp-up
items.quote: we have seen an uptick in the revenue, thereby pushing up our auto, non-auto ratio also moving from 60:40 to now we are looking at 65:35.

items.statement: Focusing on premiumization: stainless steel fasteners, higher efficiency pumps, differential materials
items.quote: we are also looking at premiumization in terms of our products of the various verticals of Sundram Fasteners we are looking at premiumization, like stainless steel fasteners and improved pumps with higher efficiencies, filtered path with two material, differential material.

items.statement: Domestic revenue split: 70% domestic, 30% export; of domestic, 55-58% OEM (35-40% CV, 40% PV)
items.quote: typically if you look at Sundram's revenue, roughly 70% of the revenue comes from the domestic market and 30% from the exports. And out of that 70%, between 55% to 58% would come from the OEM segment, and there our exposure in terms of CV between M&HCV, LCV would be close to 35% to 40%, and passenger cars would be about 40%.

items.statement: US policy uncertainty on EV subsidies may delay but not cancel OEM EV platforms
items.quote: every OEM has assured that their platforms are on, they are not going back on that. It's only a matter of time before it comes to full fruition.

items.statement: Europe export market tough; recovery expected H2 CY2025 on geopolitical stabilization
items.quote: the European market has had a very bad year, and the situation is still tough. But I think with some light at the end of the tunnel for the Israel conflict, I think things are going to settle down. And there's also hope on the Russian war front. So, Europe is expected to pick up maybe towards the second half of the year.

items.statement: North America Class 7/8 truck market expected to decline in 2025; pre-buy ahead of 2027 norms to boost H2 2025 and 2026
items.quote: the major market like commercial trucks, Class 8 or Class 7 trucks are expected to go a bit down. In fact, last year they were slightly better than expectation, but this year it's supposed to go down. And it's likely to pick up in the second half of the year, that is post-June wherein norms of '27 are going to kick in. So, from the second half of this year, and for a major portion of the next year

items.statement: Order book at Rs 43.5 billion as of Dec 24, highest in three quarters, 75% domestic
items.quote: The order backlog as of December 24th is at Rs. 43.5 billion comprising of 75% of the domestic orders.

items.statement: Order intake Rs 10.5 billion in Q3, 60% domestic, 77% bioenergy, 17% engineering, 6% PHS
items.quote: The order intake during the quarter was 10.5 billion with 60% from the domestic market. On the total order intake, 77% came from bioenergy, 17% from engineering and balance 6% from PHS business.

items.statement: International order book share at 40%, highest over last three quarters
items.quote: This quarter saw share of international order book at 40%. Our order book at this quarter also is the highest over the last three quarters.

items.statement: Service business order book for nine months FY25 trends 80% higher than entire last year
items.quote: Our order book for nine months for FY25 trends 80% higher than entire last year.

items.statement: Long-term target: 3x revenue and 5x profit by 2030 (Rs 10,000 crore topline) remains intact
items.quote: As you all know, we are embarked on an ambitious growth program for the next five years where we are aiming to grow the company three times in the top line and five times in the bottom line.

items.statement: Target 50-50 domestic-international revenue split by 2030, international to grow faster
items.quote: We have stated as part of our long-term strategy that we would like to move to a mix of 50% from domestic and 50% from international.

items.statement: Mangalore GenX facility ready with over Rs 200 crore capex and Rs 80 crore YTD opex
items.quote: The Mangalore facility is now fully ready with a total investment of over Rs. 200 crores in CAPEX and almost Rs. 80 crore YTD in form of operating expenses.

items.statement: GenX facility delayed by nearly two quarters; revenue expected from H2 FY26
items.quote: The land acquisition and readiness of the facility was delayed by nearly two quarters, which has impacted the plant business activity for the GenX business in the current year. The order book for execution from this facility is expected to start building from this quarter while the revenues will start flowing in from H2 of FY26.

items.statement: Q3 margin lower due to sales mix change (lower export execution, engineering services); 9M margin up 500 bps YoY
items.quote: The lower margin during the quarter was mainly due to the change in the sales mix. The change in the sales mix is o n account of lower export order execution and some engineering services order, which has resulted into the lower margin for the current quarter. If you compare the margin for nine months FY25, it is almost higher by 500 basis points as compared to nine months of last year

items.statement: Margin profile depends on order composition; expects positive trend on full-year basis
items.quote: On the year-end basis, on a cumulative basis, we definitely believe that our margin will show a positive trend as compared to the previous years.

items.statement: Domestic EBP20 program progressing; 18% blending expected in ethanol supply year 2024-25
items.quote: On the domestic bioenergy business front, the EBP 20 program is progressing well, and the country is expected to achieve 18% blending during ongoing ethanol supply year 2024-25.

items.statement: Starchy feedstock projects dominate ethanol space; financial closure taking longer, execution cycles extended to 16+ months
items.quote: We are witnessing starchy feedstock-based projects dominating the ethanol space. Owing to the liquidity challenges and financial closure of these projects is taking longer time leading to extension of average execution cycles moving from 12 months to 16 months and beyond.

items.statement: International bioenergy inquiry pipeline strong; US E15 year-round in 8 states, Brazil 30% blending law, Argentina and Panama increasing mandates
items.quote: On the international bioenergy front, there is strong buildup of inquiry pipeline. Amongst important developments, the USA has permitted year-round sale of E15 in 8 midwestern states. Brazil has already passed the fuel of the future law, increasing ethanol blending to 30%. Argentina and Panama have announced their plans to increase their blending mandate.

items.statement: Developed patented co-products: bio-bitumen, distillers corn oil, rice protein to enhance bioenergy project viability
items.quote: Praj is focused on enhancing value for the customers and as part of this effort, we have enhanced our focus on developing core products, which has resulted in development of bio -bitumen, distillers corn o il, rice protein etc. as solutions. These co-products will significantly alter the financial viability of bioenergy projects

items.statement: Bio-bitumen used in India's first national highway at Nagpur-Mansar Bypass NH44; can replace fossil bitumen
items.quote: Last month, the Honorable Minister of Road Transport and Highway, Shri. Nitin Gadkari inaugurated India's first National Highway at the Nagpur-Mansar Bypass Project NH 44. This highway was constructed using Praj's technology-based bio-bitumen which has the potential to replace fossil-based bitumen while enhancing the financial viability of the bioenergy projects from agri-waste.

items.statement: CBG JV with BPCL approved by boards; term sheet signed, definitive agreement in 3-4 months
items.quote: Respective boards of Praj and BPCL have given approval for formation of joint venture, which will set up CBG plants across India.

items.statement: Received CBG plant order co-located in Napier Grass field; enables low water footprint and nutrient recycling
items.quote: This quarter, we received a very interesting order to set up a CBG plant to be co-located inside a Napier Grass field.

items.statement: Four CBG projects from last year under construction; commissioning expected Q1 FY26
items.quote: The four projects that you mentioned that we had announced last year are under construction now and we expect them to go into commissioning phase towards the first quarter of next year.

items.statement: IOCL 2G project commissioning progressing; two other 2G projects to go on stream this calendar year
items.quote: We are moving forward positively on commissioning of the IOCL project which is important and it's a step-wise process. So, that happening which is the good news. We will also see the two other projects in the country go on stream during this calendar year.

items.statement: Tanzania ENA plant order won on sugary feedstock; international bioenergy expanding
items.quote: During this quarter, we w on a significant contract from a customer in Tanzania to set up ENA plant based on sugary feedstock

items.statement: Engineering business: large inquiries exist for Mangalore facility; none lost despite delays
items.quote: All opportunities are there and we think that it will definitely move forward.

items.statement: CEO Shishir Joshipura superannuating 30 June 2025; Ashish Gaikwad appointed MD-Designate effective 3 Feb 2025 for 5 years
items.quote: Shishir has been steering for last seven years, and now he's superannuating on 30th June 25. The smooth transition and succession planning for key positions for board has in its meeting held yesterday, has approved the appointment of Mr. Ashish Gaikwad as Managing Director - Designate for a period of five years, with effect from February 03.

items.statement: Cash in hand Rs 6.4 billion as of 31 Dec 2024
items.quote: Cash in hand as on 31st December is Rs. 6.4 billion.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 73% bioenergy, 18% engineering, 9% PHS; exports 21% of Q3 revenue
items.quote: Export revenues accounted for 21% in this quarter. And on the total revenue, 73% is from bioenergy, 18% from engineering business, and 9% from PHS business.

items.statement: US IRA 45Z tax credits likely for SAF producers not ethanol; SAF mandate intact from Jan 1 2027
items.quote: The SAF story is still intact. It's an international agreement that is in force that will come on 1st January 27 and will start to play out from there.

items.statement: Deposit growth guidance maintained at 9-11% for FY25
items.quote: To sum up on the guidance, we keep the deposit guidance the same at 9 to 11%.

items.statement: Advance growth guidance maintained at 11-13% for FY25
items.quote: The advanced guidance continues to be 11% to 13%.

items.statement: NIM guidance revised to 3.00-3.10% for FY25 with upside bias
items.quote: The margin guidance is 3 to 3.10% that is 3.05 +/-5 bps. With a condition that we think can come, can be positively upward also.

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance retained at 1-1.25% for FY25
items.quote: The slippage ratio continues to be 1% to 1.25%.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance retained at below 0.75% for FY25
items.quote: The credit cost continues to be the guidance of less than 0.75%.

items.statement: Nine-month NIM at 3.08%, down from 3.14% YoY due to higher deposit costs and accounting change
items.quote: Yield on advances, nine months ended, it has grown from 8.44% to 8.46%, however, there is an increase in the cost of deposit from 4.85% to 5.09%, as a result of which, the net interest margin for the nine months, as has come down a little bit from 3.14% to 3.08%.

items.statement: Penal interest accounting change impacted NIM by 5-6 bps negatively
items.quote: There was a change in accounting from penal interest and penal charges. So, that impact is almost 5 to 6 bps lower.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 2.43% (down 65 bps YoY), NNPA at 0.59%, PCR at 93.51%
items.quote: Bank enjoys a robust asset quality, healthy asset quality with gross NPA trending at 2.43%, which has reduced by 65 bps YoY. Similarly, net NPA also reduced from 0.7% to 0.59% and provision coverage ratio is robust at 93.51%.

items.statement: Quarterly slippage ratio at 0.90%, nine-month at 0.81%, both below guidance
items.quote: One of the key parameters is slippage ratio. Slippage ratio, we could improve to 0.90%against our guidance of 1 to 1.25%.

items.statement: Quarterly credit cost at 0.30%, nine-month at 0.47%, collection efficiency 99%
items.quote: we enjoy a very healthy credit cost of 0.30%, which has again improved from 0.39%. If we look at nine months period, the slippage ratio has come down to 0.81% and credit cost is 0.47%.

items.statement: SMA book (incl. restructured) at 2.48% of loans; CRILC SMA down to 0.19% after rollback of 3 accounts
items.quote: SMA book is including restructured around 28,400 crore, which is 2.48% of the total loan book.

items.statement: Domestic advances grew 11.9% YoY; Retail 20%, Agriculture 13%, MSME 14%, Corporate 7%
items.quote: Segment wise if we analyze, we continue to grow our retail, it's an organic growth of around 20%. Agriculture is growing at 13%. MSME at 14%, which is better than the previous quarters, corporate at 7%.

items.statement: Retail loan growth: Mortgage 16.3%, Home loan 16.6%, Education 17%, Auto 21%, Personal loan 24%
items.quote: If we look at the retail segment, we have seen a smart growth of around 16.3% in mortgage, 16.6% at home loan, education at 17%, auto loan at 21%, and personal loan continuously we are moderating the growth and as of December 24, we have grown at 24%.

items.statement: RAM (Retail, Agri, MSME) share improved 200 bps YoY to 59.9% of loan book
items.quote: If you look at the percentage of RAM in December 24 over December 23, it has improved by 200 bps from 57.9 to 59.9%.

items.statement: Deposits grew 11.8% YoY; CD ratio at 84.24%; CASA grew 6.5% YoY, ratio maintained ~40%
items.quote: Deposit remains a constraint for the banking industry at large. However, the Bank has grown deposit at 11.8% YoY. CD ratio is a little elevated to 84.24%. But the two noticeable aspect is that our CASA has grown YoY by 6.5%, which is better than the peer banks, and we could maintain our CASA ratio around 40% as per our guidance.

items.statement: Bulk deposits increased slightly to fund growth; CD component 25-28% of bulk deposits
items.quote: The number that you're looking at, 2,44,000, there is almost 25%-28% component of certificate of deposit therein.

items.statement: Borrowings rose to ~1.3 lakh crore; raised 15,000 crore infra bonds YTD; using refinance from NABARD/SIDBI
items.quote: Put together this financial year, we have raised infra bond to the extent of 15,000 crores and we also, you know, tap time-to-time the competitive refi from some of the domestic specialized distributions.

items.statement: Operating profit 7,664 crore (+9.3% YoY); PAT 4,837 crore (+5.6% YoY); ROA 1.15%, ROE 17%
items.quote: Bank enjoys a robust profitability and we have posted operating profit of 7,664 crore for the quarter with 9.3% YoY growth and continuously we are posting profit after tax of more than 4,000 crores and this quarter also we have posted a profit after tax of 4,837 crores with YoY growth of 5.6%.

items.statement: Nine-month operating profit +6.3%, PAT +12.6%, ROA improved to 1.17%
items.quote: If you look at the nine months period, operating profit has grown by 6.3%, profit after tax 12.6%, return on asset has improved from 1.15% to 1.17%.

items.statement: Core fee income grew 12.6% YoY; focus on optimizing fee income amid digital shift
items.quote: If you look at the core fee income this quarter, the growth is 12.6% and that is where we have to optimize that.

items.statement: Personal loan GNPA rose ~50 bps QoQ to ~3.9%; absolute slippage ~100 crore vs normalized 2,500 crore quarterly
items.quote: Actually, if you look at the GNPA that we announced for the personal loan, the book is small, let's say 32,000 crore and the GNPA for December and September there is almost a 0.5% increase on the GNPA.

items.statement: Gold loan GNPA rose from 0.71% to 0.80%; absolute amount ~36 crore; book ~6,000 crore
items.quote: Similarly, gold loan, if you take the absolute amount in terms of the 0.71 to 0.80% amount transferred to 36 crores, so that also insignificant in that way.

items.statement: No RBI guideline on collateral-free agri gold loans up to 2 lakh; MSME collateral-free up to 10 lakh being followed
items.quote: In fact, Agri gold, there is no such guideline till date, but yes on MSME there is guideline that up to 10 lakhs we can't take any collateral.

items.statement: Retail gold loan bullet repayment/LTV norms not finalized; bank compliant with current rules
items.quote: As far as the retail gold, my book is almost hardly 6,000 crores. So, it's not a very significant amount therein, but then some of the conversation we are not aware as in today, but our business is a compliant business as on today.

items.statement: Employee provisions increased due to gratuity discount rate change from 6.99% to 7.05%

items.statement: India domestic business expected to grow at mid-teens backed by strong volume growth

items.statement: Azmarda trending at ~130,000 units/month (up from 95-100k); YTD MAT ~70 crore; expect mid-teen growth

items.statement: Sporlac >120 crore annual run rate; new variants (Sporlac DG, liquid, women's health) launching in coming months

items.quote: The quantum of CAPEX is not much. We can easily absorb that as part of our regular expansion and maintenance CAPEX. So, this does not lead into any incremental CAPEX levels beyond our current steady-state level.

items.statement: Progressive portfolio (growing faster than IPM) now 65% of domestic business vs 35% four years ago; 25 brands >25 crore revenue (5 in top 150)

items.quote: MTM Forex impact of Rs. 4 crore was recorded in Quarter 3, primarily due to depreciation in ruble currency.

items.statement: Continue to evaluate assets for inorganic growth; focus on synergistic, quality assets with good payback in existing categories

items.quote: We are favorably placed for an order that amounts to something around INR60 crores, INR7O-odd crores.

items.quote: But I would say that maybe from FY '27 onwards, we can see significant revenues in this business.

items.quote: According to CEA, the power transmission sector is expected to witness investments of INR9.15 lakh crores by 2032 with interstate transmission line additions projected to grow by 30%.

items.quote: So we have moved into new tax regime. And currently, we are taxed at 25.17%, including surcharge.

items.quote: No, not at all. We don't see any demand challenge. There's plenty of opportunities everywhere in the world right now.

items.statement: Capacity constraints limiting order intake; fully booked for next 1.5-2 years

items.quote: As you see, our EBITDA margin has grown 13% from 9.39% to 10.57%. Our PAT margin has increased by 28% from 289 lakhs to 370 lakhs.

items.quote: We are planning to move into a new office. We are expanding our staff housing facility in Bellary, because we see a lot of development coming in the steel segment in Bellary.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute 40-50% of revenue; concentration seen as opportunity in oil & gas refinery segment
items.quote: Around 40 to 50%, that is what from top 10 customers, Sir.

items.quote: The book debts right now stands with the CC limit include 7 crores which is Long term debt.

items.quote: So in most of the projects we have milestone based payments. in a contract, there is material, and there is services involved. items.statement: Expanding into Saudi Arabia; close to significant deal; Nigeria operations healthy with ~20% net margin, Rs 2 crore receivable outstanding (down from Rs 3 crore)
items.quote: We are expanding into Saudi Arabia, and we are very close to striking a significant deal in in that region which will have lot of hope for growth in that part of the world.

items.statement: Team size increased from ~850 to 1,100-1,200 post-IPO; partnering with ITIs and colleges to address skilled labour shortage
items.quote: In terms of numbers, Sir, we have grown from around 850 people to 1100 , 1200 team size.

items.quote: Big pipeline is in excess of 1,000 crore. Success generally is 10% to 15% And orders in excess of 50 crores. Yes, there are plenty of orders in excess of 50 crores where we've got into the higher segment.

items.statement: New segments (renewable, data centre, water, railway, T&D) targeted for healthier margins than existing refinery/steel work
items.quote: Definitely, though the reason why these areas are being explored is that they are having healthier margins than what existing projects which are available.

items.quote: we are into the consideration of the issuing a quarterly results. But as of today, we are into our internal improvement system to give you the quarterly result. So we might start from the next financial quarter but not sure.

items.statement: Election year caused partial slowdown in fund deployment; some projects delayed due to government land issues; no red flags currently
items.quote: Only thing this year being an election year. There was, I wouldn't say, a complete slowdown. But definitely there was a partial slowdown where you know the kind of deployment of fund which was there.

items.statement: No immediate fund-raise plan; will evaluate if significant opportunity arises in new geographies/sectors
items.quote: Not really. But if there is a need we'll definitely think of it. But right now there seems to be no requirement as immediately.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 60% refinery, 20% steel, 20% other sectors; scope remains electrical/instrumentation/automation across new sectors
items.quote: We have 60% of the revenue coming from the refinery, 20% from steel and other 20% from the other sectors.

items.statement: Avoiding subcontracting route; bidding directly for new sector projects to ensure better operational efficiency
items.quote: We are avoiding the route of subcontracts. We are trying to get associated directly with the client in in order to ensure better operational efficiency.

items.statement: Old Mumbai office to be rented out, generating rental income
items.quote: Yeah, definitely, these office, in which we are existing working? It will be rented out.

items.statement: Net profit margin improved to 11.2%, up 105 bps YoY
items.quote: The net profit margin has improved to 11.2, a year-on-year growth of 105 basis points, indicating our strong bottom-line performance.

items.statement: H2 FY25 revenue expected better than H1; EBITDA and net margins to be maintained or improve slightly
items.quote: It will be in the same way. Definitely better top line compared to H1. And in line with what we have been doing, performing the same EBITDA and net margins. So, the percentage will definitely be maintained and may improve a bit.

items.quote: That currently we will follow, we see this continuing in this range. We are definitely working hard to achieve better results. So, yes, we are definitely hoping to do better also.

items.quote: So, we are currently utilizing around 80% of our capacity and keeps on fluctuating between 75 to 85. And we are targeting to reach around 90% plus in the coming quarter or maybe in the next half year or so.

items.quote: So, as we have mentioned in our IPO plan that we are expanding our existing plant capacity at our Pithampur works, whereby we are going to extend our existing plant and machinery and by installing newer larger size capacity in machines in order to cater to the ongoing projects which are there on hand with the existing customers.

items.statement: Sheet metal capacity started at 150 tons/annum, expandable to 400-500 tons at Pithampur plant
items.quote: See, currently we have started with our captive requirement. So, this is in tune of around currently 150 tons per annum and this can be expanded up to 400-500 tons.

items.statement: Diversified into sheet metal manufacturing for backward integration; initially captive, later for new customers

items.statement: 90% customers are Tier 1 OEMs; meet ~50% of plastic/rubber parts requirement for key OEMs like ZF
items.quote: We are registered vendors. 90% of our customers are in that space.

items.statement: Not in passenger vehicle segment currently; open to entry

items.statement: Strong demand for precision engineered plastic components in automotive, industrial, packaging
items.quote: The demand for precision engineered plastic components remains strong and we are well-positioned to capitalize on this.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility averaged out; managed via customer negotiations and cost reduction

items.statement: Suppliers are predetermined, standardized, approved; vendor changes require long qualification process
