items.statement: Consolidated net debt/equity 1.58x as of 31 Dec 2024
items.quote: This translates to net debt to equity of 1.58 times.

items.statement: Received Rs 108 crore from Andhra Pradesh for Canal Upgradation Project in Q3 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, we have received Rs. 108 crores from the Government of Andhra Pradesh towards work done for the Canal Upgradation Project.

items.statement: Disqualification reduced from 12 to 4 months; eligible to bid for MoRTH/NHAI/NHIDCL from 18 Feb 2025
items.quote: As per the MORTH Order dated 6 February 2025, the disqualification imposed on the Company and its two subsidiaries has been reduced from 12 months to 4 months. Accordingly, we will resume participation in the bidding processes of MoRTH, NHAI and NHIDCL from 18 February 2025 onwards.

items.statement: Targeting monetization of 11 of 12 assets by 31 Mar 2025 (10 HAM + 1 BOT toll), equity invested Rs 1,620 crore; last asset by Q1/Q2 FY26
items.quote: we are targeting 11 assets this year before end of financial year, monetization and the closure and the transfer of asset before 31 st March, 11 assets out of 12. And the remaining asset may be in the Q1 of FY26 or latest by Q2?

items.statement: Expected equity valuation ~1.67x invested equity at signing of share purchase agreement
items.quote: Earlier we have given in our note, about 1.67 times of the equity invested at the time of signing of the share purchase agreement.

items.statement: JJM revenue guidance: FY25 Rs 800-850 crore, FY26 ~Rs 1,200 crore, balance completion by FY27
items.quote: This year, already we achieved more than Rs. 600 crores. So, we are expecting total guidance for the current financial year would be between Rs. 800 crores to Rs. 850 crores. And the next financial year, we are expecting some expedited progress. And it would be around Rs. 1,200 crores in the next financial year.

items.statement: Irrigation revenue guidance: Q4 FY25 Rs 50-60 crore, FY26 Rs 400-450 crore, completion by FY27
items.quote: And the next one and a half months we should be able to get around Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores project. And in the next financial year we are expecting around Rs. 400 crores to Rs. 450 crores revenue from the irrigation project.

items.statement: Land acquisition delays and procedural issues caused low awarding in past 1.5 years; now improving with arbitration awards and circle rate revisions
items.quote: Because of elections in Bihar, elections in Maharashtra , d ue to which there were some problems internally. Now it seems that in Bharatmala, they couldn't get land, so Bharat mala stopped. The contracts awarded two years ago, after that, they couldn't do it again. Now they have started that contract again like our Bihar project, which is part of Bharat mala, Varanasi to Kolkata

items.statement: Indian GDP growth slowed but rural consumption strong; tax cuts and rate cuts support discretionary auto demand
items.quote: The Indian GDP has slowed down a little as compared to the last year, but still remains strong as compared to the modest global growth. The rural consumption has remained strong in the past few quarters. The income tax cut by the government in the budget and interest rate reduction by the Central Bank augurs well for India as it will help in further improving the consumption of the discretionary g

items.statement: 2-wheeler grew 8%, PV 2.8%, CV degrew 1.8%, 3-wheeler degrew 2.6% YoY; QoQ all segments degrew except CV
items.quote: During quarter 3 of FY '25, the 2-wheeler, 3-wheeler and passenger vehicle segments registered moderate growth, whereas commercial vehicles and 3-wheelers showed degrowth on a year-on-year basis. 2 -wheelers grew by 8%, passenger vehicles grew by 2.8%, comm ercial vehicles degrew by 1.8% and 3 -wheelers degrew by 2.6%. However, on a quarter -on-quarter basis, we saw degrowth in almost all segments

items.statement: NCLT approved amalgamation of Varroc Polymer with Varroc Engineering effective 1 April 2024; exceptional cost INR112.7 million for stamp duties
items.quote: Firstly, the company received NCLT approval for amalgamation of Varroc Polymer Limited with Varroc Engineering Limited effective 1st April, 2024. The effects of amalgamation are considered in the stand -alone financial statements. An exceptional cost of INR112.7 million is recognized towards estimated costs like stamp duties directly attributable to this merger.

items.statement: China JV classified as assets held for sale post arbitration verdict requiring stake sale for RMB 310.5 million; exceptional cost INR796.5 million recognized
items.quote: Secondly, the China joint venture has been recognized as assets held for sale post the arbitration verdict, which requires us to sell the stake to the JV partner in lieu of RMB 310.5 million. An exceptional cost of INR796.5 million is recognized since the net realization, including the estimated taxes and other expenses will be lower than the carrying value of the investment.

items.statement: Revenue INR20,753 million, up 10.1% YoY; EBITDA flat at 9.2% YoY, down 50 bps QoQ due to higher tooling costs
items.quote: The company registered a revenue of INR20,753 million with a growth of 10.1% year -on-year. Various new programs which we won in the past period moved to production during the quarter. Thus the tooling sales in this quarter was much higher. On the other hand, higher tooling costs had a one -time impact on our gross margin. Despite that, our EBITDA on a year -on-year basis remained the same at 9.2%

items.statement: PBT before exceptional items and JV improved 80 bps YoY due to lower depreciation and interest from capex control and free cash flow generation
items.quote: Our PBT before exceptional items and JV has improved by 80 basis points on a year -on-year, mainly due to control on capex and generation of free cash flow, which is resulting in lower depreciation and interest costs.

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR1,967 million in 9M FY25 to INR7,860 million; net debt/equity 0.5x from 0.64x at end FY24
items.quote: The net debt of the company in 9 months FY '25 reduced by INR1,967 million and net debt to equity reduced to 0.5x at the end of 9 months of FY '25 from 0.64x at the end of FY '24. The absolute net debt figure was INR7,860 million.

items.statement: Annualized ROCE at 19.3% at end of 9M FY25
items.quote: The annualized ROCE at the end of the 9 months of FY '25 was at 19.3%.

items.statement: 9M FY25 net new business wins with annualized peak revenue INR10,847 million; EV models >55% of wins
items.quote: The order book for 9 months of FY '25 has further strengthened and we continue to build the order book in both India and in the overseas business. In 9 months of FY '25, we have achieved net new business wins with annualized peak revenues of INR10,847 million. The order book from EV models constitutes more than 55% of these wins.

items.statement: Two large overseas wins: front/rear drive inverter electronics and interior ambient lighting for electric passenger vehicle; SOP FY27
items.quote: We have 2 big business wins in our overseas operations. First one is front drive and rear drive inverter electronics for the electric passenger vehicle. The second one is the interior am bient lighting. The start of production will take place from FY '27.

items.statement: India win: power electronics (traction motors and controller) for 3-wheeler player; SOP next calendar year
items.quote: In the Indian operation, the order book, which is worth mentioning is a win for power electronics that is traction motors and controller for a 3-wheeler player. The SOP of this will happen in the next calendar year.

items.statement: EV-related products revenue ~10.5% of total revenue in Q3 and 9M FY25
items.quote: Another important point here is similar to what we indicated earlier, the revenue from EV-related products comes to about 10.5% of revenue now. And if you take 9 months together also, it's pretty close to 10%.

items.statement: FY25 capex INR260-270 crore including land; FY26 regular capex INR200-250 crore plus ~INR150 crore for land
items.quote: So our regular capex will be just about INR200 crores plus we are also investing in land for this year. So finally, we may end up this year with about INR260 crores to INR270 crores. Next year also, the regular capex will be in the range of maybe INR200 crores to INR250 crores. But next year, again, if required, we may have to invest something in the land. So that's where it is.

items.statement: Additional ~INR150 crore land capex planned for FY26 in Pune or northern region for 7-8 years capacity
items.quote: Other than the INR250 crores, INR200 crores, INR250 crores for normal capex for some growth capex, we will I think have to budget next year at least I think close to INR150 crores at least of capex towards land because that's something which will be important, which can again last us for the next 7, 8 years at least.

items.statement: Target FY25 year-end net debt ~INR700 crore; China realization (INR320-330 crore net) will further reduce debt
items.quote: Debt reduction, I think you've seen the number. We are right now at INR786 crores. So like what we indicated earlier, we may end this year with somewhere around INR700 crores to be the number. This is without considering the China realization. China realization when it comes, obviously, it will be less to that extent.

items.statement: China JV sale net realization expected INR320-330 crore after ~10% capital gains tax and costs; 45-day period overdue but discussions ongoing
items.quote: Coming to the net realization, of course, the tax impact is still under discussion. But based on whatever opinion we got, I think there will be a 10% capital gains tax, which will be taken as withholding tax reduction, plus some cost and all. So broadly around INR320 crores to INR330 crores of net realization is what we should see.

items.statement: Romania electronics facility at 15-20% utilization; utilization to rise from July 2026, peak revenue ~USD30 million annually
items.quote: so see, what we are looking at -- now you said 3 businesses. See one is, of course, the electronics business out of Romania, which today, I mean, is very much underutilized probably at about 15%, 20% utilization, that we will start seei ng utilization going up from July of '26 and then reach -- in some months, it will reach that peak of $30 million annually

items.statement: Overseas new programs capex USD2-3 million; most infrastructure already in place
items.quote: So in terms of the capex, we are expecting this to be -- I don't want to give you some wrong numbers, but essentially in the range of $2 million to $3 million.

items.statement: Premium 2-wheeler lighting revenue flat next 12 months; new premium customer win EUR3 million/year starting FY27; Vietnam growth expected from FY27
items.quote: So there, the larger customer has been so far over the years, Piaggio and we have seen some fall in sales with Piaggio. So going forward, we see sales in the next financial year to be similar in 2-wheeler lighting as the current year. But of course, the 2-wheeler lighting on a whole is profitable. But we won orders already from one premium customer with a large order I mean, revenue size of almost

items.statement: IMES challenged this year due to Caterpillar volume decline; targeting PBT neutral next year with revenue recovery from April and new customer discussions
items.quote: We are expecting that next year, we should have a higher level of revenues. We've already seen some revenues go up from January, but it's not enough. So we do expect higher level of revenues from April overall. So with that level of revenues, I mean, our b asic objective is that we try to reach at least a PBT neutral kind of a situation instead of a PBT negative which is there today in this financ

items.statement: No plan to divest IMES currently; focus on making it profitable first as no buyers in current state
items.quote: So presently, see, the point is, I agree with you, it's not a part of a core business. But in the current situation, current state, there won't be any buyers in this current state. And therefore, I think it is prudent as a company that we focus on increasi ng sales because the plant is actually quite good and the current customers also are very happy. The question is of sales. We have enough capac

items.statement: Employee expense QoQ increase due to severance pay overseas and prior provision reversals; restructuring from March to reduce headcount; sustainable run rate near current level with merit increases offset by headcount reduction
items.quote: This quarter, we also had some severance pay in some of these overseas locations. That's more like a one -timer. Plus last quarter, we also had certain credits, certain reversals of provision reversals, which we took. So because of that, the quarter-over-quarter will appear to be a big variance. Going forward, yes, we are also doing some kind of restructuring currently. So that will bring in some

items.statement: Tooling sales impact ~0.4% on gross margin QoQ (Q3 vs Q2); inventory correction and base effects explain remaining YoY gap
items.quote: See, tooling generally go with a lower margin than the regular product. So if you see the impact -- I mean, if you really see this quarter margin -- gross margin with last quarter, I think close to about 0.4% is because of the tooling sale impact.

items.statement: Margins expected to improve next year from cost optimization, renewable energy Phase 2, interest savings from debt reduction, and stable depreciation; no numeric guidance given
items.quote: It should certainly be better. We don't want to put a number and give a guidance to it. But yes, you're right, there are various actions which are in progress, the cost optimization things and we are also doing a Phase 2 in renewable energy, plus interest saving itself should be significant if we really end this year with below INR700 crores. Then similarly, depreciation should more or less stabil

items.statement: Integrated starter motor (ISG) has 2 customers (1 in SOP, 1 in development); ~15-20% value increase vs standalone starter motor
items.quote: So stand-alone, I would say, probably around at least 15-ish -- somewhere between 15% to 20% value increase.

items.statement: India self-sufficient in lighting technology; will maintain China engineering team for 4-wheeler lighting and ADAS electronics post JV sale
items.quote: I think one, from an India perspective, I think we are self -sufficient anyway in India, especially for the technology level required. And further for the future level of technology also required, I think whether across China or other parts of the world, broadly, we are protected. So we don't see any risk. We do want to maintain a level of engineering in China for our 4-wheeler lighting, especiall

items.statement: 4-wheeler lighting domestic traction: decent order book, recent full LED headlamp localization for a customer
items.quote: I would say, we have a decently sized book of business. We continue to win business. We continue to deliver. I think most recently, we have executed -- we supported a customer with the localization of a full -fledged LED headlamp, which has been completely indigenized. So like with any, I would say, there is a good level of traction based on the service that we offer.

items.statement: Strong portfolio across all powertrains (ICE, EV, CNG); ICE products like engine valves growing due to competitor exits, not cannibalized by EV
items.quote: Also to add, actually, see, today, even the current products like engine valves and all, there's a huge demand for these kind of products. Now today, in fact, we're in a situation where we don't have capacity to actually offer to the customers. There's so much of demand because some of the people have exited this business. So there's a lot of demand and pressure on us to deliver. So that's not a b

items.statement: 9M FY25 revenue INR59.74 billion lifetime value, annual peak revenue INR10.85 billion; 53% EV-related wins; overseas wins shift mix to 37% 4-wheeler, 56% EV, 68.66% non-Bajaj
items.quote: In terms of the lifetime business won in 9 months, it was coming to INR59.74 billion with annual peak revenue potential of INR10.85 billion. The interesting point here is 53% of the business win is relating to the EV vehicles. This includes a significant win in overseas operations from a reputed OEM. So this will be operational or this will be starting production during FY '27.

items.statement: Targets 15-20% revenue growth and 16-18% EBITDA margin for coming quarters
items.quote: We feel that our EBITDA margins should remain between 16% to 18%. That's what we are targeting to maintain. And revenues, we feel that we should be able to grow between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Export demand stable but prices subdued; domestic demand strong with 30% volume growth
items.quote: The export market demand is more or less stable. We are getting demand inquiries, but the prices are slightly subdued. That is the situation now.

items.statement: Export prices declined 15% YoY in Q3, 20% YoY in Q2; QoQ prices now stable
items.quote: Y-o-Y, the price has declined on an average by around 15%. And in last quarter, average decline was around 20%.

items.statement: Current prices well below 2019 levels, some products down over 50%
items.quote: Sir, the prices now have settled at much below the 2019 level. They have not reached the 2019 level at all.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 16.7% in Q3, down due to employee, freight, job work costs; gross margin stable
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 16.7% in Q3 FY '25. Our gross margin remained stable. However, EBITDA margin declined due to employee expenses to upgrade talent pool and R&D capability, rise in ocean freight costs and higher job work related expenses due to increased volume.

items.statement: Hamirpur capex ~INR50 cr/year, 2 blocks in FY26, 10-12 blocks long-term; Sandila near saturation
items.quote: We are doing capex on an annual basis around INR50 crores in our Hamirpur site. So, we will be keeping on getting the revenue generated. Every year, that will be increasing.

items.statement: Sandila utilization ~60% in 9M FY25; Hamirpur to start contributing FY26, full ramp FY27
items.quote: It will be around 60%.

items.statement: Signed 3-year contract for pharma intermediate supplies to Japanese companies, next shipment by March/April
items.quote: We already have signed a 3-year contract with them. And our next supplies would be in, I think, by March end or April second week.

items.statement: Domestic portfolio expanded to fungicides/herbicides with >75% and ~50% market share; realizations ~INR400-450/kg
items.quote: In the domestic market, we are working on some few fungicides and some herbicides and we are very well placed in that. And there, our market share is almost more than 75% in one product.

items.statement: Hamirpur to add new products only: one intermediate, one insecticide, one herbicide; prices ~INR1,200-1,300/kg
items.quote: At Hamirpur side, the prices would be slightly different because at that price, the product what we are targeting at Hamirpur would be around INR1,200 to INR1,300 a kg.

items.statement: Top 10 customer share fell from 61% to 42% due to product mix change; MNC customers now order 1-2 months ahead vs 3-6 months earlier
items.quote: Now our MNC customer, they are not keeping stock with themselves. They are giving orders now for only 1 month in advance. Earlier they used to give orders in 3 months to 6 months in advance with good planning.

items.statement: Inventory days ~170 due to herbicide stock build for Kharif; expected to rationalize by 20-25 days from Q4
items.quote: Inventory number of days is slightly higher. They will be around 170 days, since we have started building up inventory for one of the herbicide to be sold in next Kharif season.

items.statement: All capex funded from internal accruals; no term loans taken; subsidiary may take nominal debt later
items.quote: Yes, yes. We have not taken any term loan till date right now.

items.statement: Exports INR75 cr in Q3 (down from INR87 cr); US ~15% of exports (~INR50 cr); Europe and Australia major markets
items.quote: Exports to U.S. market has grown, but it will be around, say, 15% of our export turnover.

items.statement: 69% raw materials sourced locally; backward integration to continue at same level
items.quote: It will be more or less same. It will be more or less in the same range because we are trying to integrate backward as much as possible.

items.statement: Budget 2025-26 initiatives (PM Dhan-Dhanya Krishi Yojana, National Manufacturing Mission) seen as positive for sector
items.quote: The Union Budget '25-'26 has introduced several initiatives that are poised to positively impact our sector.

items.statement: US tariff threats creating uncertainty; Chinese capacity closures expected as prices below cost
items.quote: That is true, sir, because of the present situation of the threats received from U.S. President about the tariffs. So the whole situation is slightly getting complicated.

items.statement: Volume growth ~30% YoY in Q3; 9M FY25 revenue INR633 cr (+12%), EBITDA INR101 cr (+6.3%), EBITDA margin 15.9%
items.quote: Overall, sales volume has increased by around 30% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Aspires to achieve 17-19% EBITDA margin, not specifically for FY25 but as a medium-term target
items.quote: We still very much on track with 17% to 19% as guided earlier in terms of EBITDA margin, and 16.2% has delivered in this quarter is, good step up towards that number.

items.statement: A&P spend expected to trend at 7-7.5% of revenue for the full year, flat in absolute terms YoY
items.quote: Our overall numbers for the year will be trending in a similar range, like 7% - 7.5% is what we have been trending at, and we don't see any increase in A&P spend for the entire year.

items.statement: No significant addition to employee headcount or cost anticipated in short to medium term
items.quote: We don't anticipate any significant addition to the employee either head count or the cost overall.

items.statement: Q3 revenue grew 9.1% YoY to INR 514.8 cr, highest ever quarterly revenue, driven by distribution and online growth
items.quote: We achieved the highest ever quarterly revenues of INR 514.8 crores, largely attributed to our aggressive distribution drive strategy and our high online sales benefiting from the festive season.

items.statement: Volume grew 10% YoY to 7.6 million pairs in Q3, ASP flat at INR 683 for footwear, overall ASP down 1% to INR 675 due to accessories mix
items.quote: The company sold approximately 7.6 million pairs in Q3 FY25 up 10% year-on-year. The average selling price stood at around INR 675, in Q3 FY25 a drop of 1% year-on-year, driven by higher saliency of accessories and socks. Footwear ASP remained flat at INR 683 per pair.

items.statement: Gross margin 51.2% in Q3, down 20 bps YoY and 140 bps QoQ due to raw material inflation, adverse mix, and BIS inventory liquidation
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter was at 51.2% versus 51.4% in quarter three FY24 showing a drop of 20 bps, marginally lower, driven by raw material price increases. On a quarter-on-quarter basis also our gross margin dropped by 140 basis points driven by raw material price increase, adverse mix and liquidation of non-moving BIS inventory.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 440 bps YoY to 16.6% in Q3 due to normalized SG&A and lower provisioning
items.quote: EBITDA margin has expanded by 440 bps Y-o-Y, from 12.2% to 16.6% primarily due to improvement in debtors and inventory health, which is basically lower provisioning, reflecting better working capital management.

items.statement: BIS inventory liquidation impact 20-40 bps on gross margin over last three quarters, less than 10% of finished goods inventory remains non-BIS
items.quote: So as far as the BIS inventory liquidation is concerned, that impact is in the range of anywhere between 20 to 40 bps, depending on in the last three quarters. So, it varies depending on article-to-article.

items.statement: Expect majority of non-BIS inventory liquidated by March end, Q4 impact only 10-20 bps
items.quote: It would not be a significant number as we said that the inventory levels are very low. The non-BIS inventory levels are very low as of now. So, there could be a 10 or 20 bps impact. That's what we foresee, we don't see any material number there.

items.statement: TPU price increase due to countervailing and customs duty; selective price hikes of 7-10% taken in Nov and Jan in less price-sensitive categories to insulate P&L
items.quote: This quarter we saw one of the component called TPU price increase primarily due to countervailing duty imposed, customs duty imposed. It was a conscious call on our behalf not to pass on the prices to consumers. But we have taken selective price increases in November and also in Jan beginning.

items.statement: Price hikes targeting overall 2-3% impact to offset raw material inflation
items.quote: Yes, as I said that the idea is to insulate the P&L from the input price increase or inflation, that's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Sneaker ASP 15-20% higher than current revenue base, margin accretive despite higher cost
items.quote: So, this would be at least 15% to 20% higher versus our current revenue based. Prerna Jhunjhunwala: Sorry, sir continue. Sanjay Chhabra: Of course it would also have a higher cost component, but net, net it would be margin accretive

items.statement: Gannaur sole manufacturing unit CAPEX completed in Q3; Haridwar upper manufacturing facility completion expected Q4 FY25 with commercial production from March 2025
items.quote: The CAPEX for the sole manufacturing unit at our Gannaur facility was completed in Q3 FY25. Furthermore, we anticipate the completion of our Haridwar facility dedicated for manufacturing state of the art uppers in Q4 FY25 with commercial production projected to commence from March 2025.

items.statement: Haridwar unit to add 2.4 million pairs of sneaker capacity; currently under 10% volume share in sneakers
items.quote: We would be adding around 2.4 million pairs of sneaker capacity through our Haridwar new unit. Currently we are under 10% in terms of volume share, and with the new capacity addition, we definitely expect to ramp up further.

items.statement: Added 6 new EBOs in Q3, total 290; entered Zepto for quick commerce; gaining traction in premium large format stores
items.quote: During the quarter, we have added six new stores across India, taking our total EBO count to 290. We have embarked our presence on Zepto during the end of the quarter, thereby satiating our customers presence with prompt delivery convenience through quick commerce.

items.statement: EBO addition strategy 40-50 stores per year, more selective on geography; distribution reach expanded 7-8% in Q3 with throughput per outlet improving
items.quote: Our strategy would continue to be 40 to 50 stores addition in the year. And as far as distribution is concerned, please appreciate this quarter three is both festival season and also seasonality in the North. So the retail touch point addition is highest in quarter three, having said that, we added around 7% to 8% retail touch points, but our sales growth was 9% to 10% so, the output or throughput

items.statement: Inventory days improved to 95 from 110 days YoY; DSO flat QoQ; distributor inventory healthy at 80-90 days; primary and secondary sales gap minimal
items.quote: On the inventory front, we have 95 days of inventory holding from 110 days last year. So there also we have seen our whatever numbers we are targeting in terms of driving inventory days, we are able to achieve that. So don't see any stress in working capital.

items.statement: Distributor inventory at 84 days via DMS, within internal norms of 60-90 days; no push sales, replenishment model working
items.quote: And that 84 days level through our DMS, the inventory levels are very much within our internal norms of 60 to 90 days.

items.statement: Company has become debt-free, improving EBITDA to PAT conversion
items.quote: EBITDA to PAT conversion has also significantly gone up as we have become debt free. So even, at 16% let's say EBITDA we have been able to deliver a good decent PAT, so the conversion is also sort of helping us there get to the PAT level.

items.statement: Declared first-ever interim dividend of INR 0.70 (~25% of YTD PAT); intends to continue dividends going forward, final dividend depends on board
items.quote: Gaurav of course the dividend, firstly we are very happy to declare the interim dividend, for the first time in the history of the company. So that does give us confidence in our ability to deliver and we would be looking, we will try to deliver dividends simply going forward, right that's the idea.

items.statement: Competitive intensity peaked last year, now normalizing; gained market share in North, West, Central, East regions despite subdued macro
items.quote: We have certainly outperformed in our key states, of the North, West and Central regions, also East. So, we do believe that we have gained, the lost ground, and there has been a good uptick in our market share.

items.statement: Government budget incentives for footwear sector expected, driven by employment generation agenda; details awaited
items.quote: Nothing has been put out on paper yet, but we do anticipate, the government has called out these certain incentives. So clearly, there is a drive and a push by the government to sort of grow the sector meaningfully, because it does generate, it is one of those sectors which generates. One of the highest employments across the country, as it is a labor intensive industry.

items.statement: Demand not fully normalized, still some pain in market; improvement from last year but not at pre-COVID levels
items.quote: The demand is not like absolutely normal in terms of how it used to be let say two years ago, or three years ago rather. It is certainly an improvement from last year in Q3 as well and Q4 also. But I don't know if the demand is, we can call it absolutely normalized demand. So, there is still some pain in the market.

items.statement: Revenue growth 9.1% YoY in Q3, 10% for 9M FY25; volume growth 10% YoY in Q3
items.quote: Our revenue from operations grew by 9.1% year-on-year to INR 515 crores in Q3 FY25, largely benefited by higher distribution, which registered a growth of around 9% and online channel which showed a revenue growth of around 11%.

items.statement: PAT grew 86.7% YoY to INR 46.5 cr in Q3; PAT margin expanded 370 bps to 9%; ROCE 22.1%, ROE 17.5% as of Dec 2024
items.quote: PAT grew by 86.7% year-on-year to INR 46.5 crore and PAT margins expanded by 370 bps year-on-year to 9%. Our balance sheet continues to demonstrate strength with robust return ratios such as return on capital employed at 22.1% and return on equity at 17.5% as of 31st December 2024.

items.statement: Expects to add ~1,000 beds in next 3.5 years, including ~400 beds in NCR (two Gurgaon hospitals) and ~600 beds in regional/spoke hospitals in South and new geographies
items.quote: We have a trajectory, which has already been discussed, of about 1,000 beds in the next 3.5 years, Sen. About 400 beds are planned for the NCR, with two hospitals already planned in Gurgaon. The remaining 600 beds will be in regional spokes as well as spoke hospitals in the south.

items.statement: FY25-26 capex for 250 leased beds at INR60-65 lakh/bed; FY26-27 capex for 130 leased beds; Gurgaon project INR400 crore over next 3 years starting FY25-26, mostly after year 1
items.quote: In FY '25-26, we are coming with 250 of the beds, and these are all asset-light, means these are leased assets. And similarly, on FY '26-27 is 130 beds. So roughly 380 beds to 400 beds, which will come in next 2 years. Since these are on the leased assets, roughly INR60 - 65 lakh per bed, you should assume on that as a capex. One concern obviously is that planting acreage in Tamil Nadu, which is on a downward trend for all players because of competitive crop scenario. So that would continue to be a concern in Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: Aspire to exit this decade with much larger CPG business and high double-digit EBITDA percentage given it's a food F&B business.

items.statement: Sugar business ~55% institutional sales, almost all value-added products; CPG value-added share ~15% of sales.
items.quote: Broadly our business today is around 55% in institutional sales and almost all of that is a value-added product. So that's the split that will be there in the sugar sales.

items.statement: CPG present in 4 Southern states for non-sweetener and sweetener; some presence in West, e-commerce, modern trade, East (modern trade only); intend to consolidate in South before expanding nationally.

We intend to stay in the South and consolidate our position for some time before we decide to move into the rest of the country.

items.statement: MSP increase for sugar requested by industry; FRP increases year-on-year not commensurate with MSP; government seized of matter, timeline uncertain.

items.quote: If I remember correctly, our EBITDA margin last quarter was also about 16%, 17%. So, to that extent, whatever exports we do to U.S., the EBITDA will come down to 10%.

items.quote: And the total capex would be, like you mentioned, between INR1,700 crores and INR1,800 crores.

items.quote: So there is always a possibility of preponing or postponing of 1 or 2 quarters for whatever reasons that somebody has. So reacting to something which is likely to h appen, let's say, 9 months, 12 months down the road is very

items.statement: Global ex-China EAF share rose from 40% to ~50% in last 5-7 years (25% jump)

items.statement: Expect minimum 20% revenue growth in FY26

items.statement: Expect to maintain or improve current EBITDA margins

items.statement: Debt maintained well below INR1,000 crores as of Q3
items.quote: We are maintaining our levels much below what we had stated and indicated to you close to -- so about INR1,000-odd crores or so.

items.quote: We are completing a lot of other regulatory compliances, including preparation of drug master files and all that. So it is a long drawn process, which would be there.

items.quote: Total in 9-months, Rs. 154 crores.

items.quote: India makes up 40% of our business, weaker than expected festive season, excess channel inventory, lower than projected government spending with spurs of rural economy and unusually weak urban spending adversely impacted our volumes, registering low single-digit decline for this quarter.

items.quote: we are clear that from Q1 '25, '26 onwards, things should start picking up as both rural and urban spending will drive the mass and masstige segment for the performance surfactants.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth guidance of 75-100% may be impacted; management says difficult to achieve 75% but still trying, will confirm by end of Q4

items.statement: Management personally feels difficult to achieve 75% growth for FY25 but still working towards it

And we have completed the entire policy changes and the cooperative banks can restart the acquiring business, that's the recent update. The new onboarding, which was completely halted, has now already begun.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 sales target close to INR12 crores to achieve FY25 30% growth target

So, these kinds of inquiries we have and we are short of frames, in fact, and we have more inquiries in pipeline for that.

items.quote: So, 90 days is something that is a cut-off line for every client to pay in time. We don't generally have an approach of shutting down our services and spoiling with the clients because they are all A-group clients which we work with.

items.statement: Bank creditworthiness top A-class; can raise additional INR50 crores if needed; warrant funds 75% pending receipt

items.quote: Obviously we have a backup with the warrants we have done already in November which was done at INR268 at that time and that fund is 75% is yet to be received.

items.quote: Right now, we don't face. Yes, there is an increased cost to it which is coming. But that is fair. I mean, with the demand is there, so there is going to be an increased cost. But it is sustainable and maintainable.

items.quote: The second is the young fleet that we have. So, we do not have very, very heavy maintenance coming on this fleet for another 5 years, at least, if I would say, because the lifespan of these cranes are generally 20, 25, 30 years.

items.statement: Supplying power to Bangladesh Power Development Board; receivables manageable and within contractual structures

items.statement: Supply power to Bhutan as per requirement with necessary approvals and infrastructure

items.statement: Buyback/dividend options from ONGC deal proceeds to be presented to Board for decision
items.quote: Your suggestion is duly noted, of course whenever we receive this money from deal, so options will be presented before the Board, and as per the decision of the Board further actions shall be taken.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue target Rs 675 crore; good chance of achieving it given 9M performance
items.quote: This is our outlook for 2024-25, as previously stated. We have set a target of Rs. 675 crores in consolidated revenue for this year. Given the output from the first nine months, we have a good chance of achieving this target.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target Rs 850 crore; FY27 target Rs 1000 crore; EBITDA margin 12-14% for next two years excluding rupee depreciation benefit
items.quote: Our target for the next two years is approximately Rs. 1000 crore. We have clearly stated that our EBITDA will be between 12-14%, without factoring in the potential impact of rupee depreciation.

items.statement: Consolidated order book Rs 933 crore as of 1 Feb; expect carry-forward orders > Rs 825 crore this year
items.quote: This is the consolidated order position as on 1st February, approximately Rs.933 crores. This is our order pipeline classified as negotiated & under negotiation pipeline, and we have negotiated approximately Rs. 26 crores worth of orders.

items.statement: Order book projected to exceed Rs 830 crore; could reach Rs 900-950 crore by year-end
items.quote: So, projection can go up to Rs900 crores. So, it's a very fragile kind of world when you talk about marketing and then we have around one and a half months left, so order, book position is extremely good and as you saw it's more than Rs.900 crores plus.

items.statement: Rs 110-120 crore capex lined up; partly internal accruals, partly term loan if needed
items.quote: Last year, we have taken around Rs. 110 crore, and we are aiming for a similar amount this year. However, if we encounter any liquidity issues, we will consider taking a term loan for further expansion. Generally, we have not taken any loans.

items.statement: Consolidated capacity utilisation ~60%; expanding Chennai plant (inauguration May 2025), SEZ Pithampur (Dec 2025), US Orange facility (+45k sq ft), Houston plant (2027)
items.quote: So, capacity utilization we are at around 60% but at the same time you will see we are expanding the facility. So, just to give you an idea we are setting up a new plant in Shivpad which my colleague Dharm endra explained, we are going to inaugurate in this May, currently in coming next 2-3

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin ~61%, EBITDA ~20%, PBT 13%, PAT 12% for 9M FY25; Q3 EBITDA and PAT margins very good
items.quote: This is consolidated revenue, overall performance, 46% increase in the turnover of nine months. Same way gross margin is around same 61%. EBITDA margin is also same 20%. Profit before tax slightly increased from 11 to 13% and profit after tax also increased from 9% to 12%.

items.statement: US manufacturing margins maintained; local US pricing includes additional price for BABA compliance

This means Jash Engineering Limited that the margins will be calculated accordingly. items.statement: Disc filter localisation cut cost from Rs 1-1.5 cr to Rs 45-50 lakh per 8-wheel unit; 98% indigenised; EBITDA margins 20-25% on recent orders
items.quote: So currently eight wheel disc filter is around just Rs.45-50 lakhs. So, you can understand that we have reduced 50% of the entire pricing, not even cost. Cost is going much down, 98% of the products utiliz e in this complete equipment is now localized, indigenized, including fabrication, all forges, machine and everything.

items.statement: UK framework expansion: accepted as supplier chain partner for United Utilities (5th largest UK water utility); already on Scottish Water and Severn Trent frameworks
items.quote: But in last few months, we are into seven trends, which is the second biggest framework authority business into UK, and we have now been just as recent as three weeks, we have been now accepted as the supplier chain partner in united utilities, which is the fifth biggest in UK.

items.statement: Galliford Try (UK's largest contractor) agreement near signing; will unlock framework access and significant order flow
items.quote: we have started an agreement which is still to be legalized, but we have already framed up a document with Galliford Try, who are one of the biggest contractors in overall UK and they have owned Ham Baker Engineering services

items.statement: US revenue target $33-35M FY25 ($15M from US facility, balance from India); targeting $40-45M from US facility next year; $50-60M by 2029

So, when you talk about an Orange component or the US component of $15 million, the $15 million is bifurcated as actuations, hydraulics and other things, are around $3 million, wherein there is no manufacturing component involved from US.

items.statement: Middle East market potential Rs 400-500 cr for gates/screens/valves; desalination alone Rs 300-500 cr; considering Saudi manufacturing facility
items.quote: So, if I talk about gates, screens, knife gate valve business only these three business, and I am currently not talking about the process equipment and other products that we have, we see that it will be around Rs.400-500 crore business in the coming future years. Currently, there is a very huge potential, desalination market itself is around Rs.300-500 crore, very huge market.

items.statement: BABA Act requires 95% US manufacturing/procurement by 2029; expanding Orange, MA facility (+45k sq ft) and planning Houston plant to comply
items.quote: If you see B ABA act the build America Buy America, which is coming out of US till 2029 that's what we see and it has been in the previous era. If you see, they have a law that by 2029 we have to manufacture more than 95%, I mean procurement of raw material to manufacturing to be done 95% in

items.statement: Debtor days 100-120, inventory days 120-140; cash conversion cycle ~150-160 days; stable for 1-2 years despite BABA projects
items.quote: Our working capital has been stable over the last two to three years, with debtor days around 100-120 and inventory days around 120 -140. With the implementation of the BABA Act, we are already engaged in projects under this act, which typically offer very good margins. As a result, there hasn't been much change in our working capital cycle, and it is expected to remain around 150-160 days.

items.statement: Skilled labour shortage globally (US, UK, Germany); hiring only junior/technician roles ($23-24/hr); top management positions filled; not doubling headcount
items.quote: So, Alisha, that is one of the rider that we see, one of the problem statement that we see, manpower availability and to be more precise, the skilled manpower availability is a serious dearth across the globe. I am traveling anywhere in Germany, US, everywhere skilled manpower is a serious concern, and we also face that in US, UK.

items.statement: Trump tariffs on metals: no impact as minimal exports from India to US; US manufacturing expansion mitigates BABA risk
items.quote: But to clear everything, I would say we don't have any impact with the Trumpian tariff system, number one. Number two, to clarify one of your question, we don't export anything from Shivpad to Rodney Hunt.

items.statement: Order-to-revenue lead time: 4-7 months for small orders, 1-2 years for large orders (>$3-4M); US Army radial gates order $6-8M with 4-year lead time
items.quote: So, it depends on the size and quantum of order. So, something between 4-7 months could be a general lead time but it still depends. Let's say US Army Corp order is there to be delivered in US, it can be one year. Currently, we are just on the verge of getting a radial gates order, which is a very big order. I would say in US value would be anything like $6-8 million and the lead time is 4 years.

items.quote: So of course, there will be no manufacturing facility in Austria. We are not thinking of that. Jash Engineering Limited But yes, Ganot will operate from Austria only, and the orders will go through Mahr

items.quote: Still not Started. Tej Patel: Okay Bhuvanesh Pandey: Definitely, we have sold screens in the past it's not that we have never sold screens. We have already sold screens, screens from India. We manufacture screens from US and have sold. So, screens is not that it's on a zero level

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 21-23% for FY25; confident of achieving despite Q3 at 23% on higher revenue base
items.quote: Sir had mentioned that we are targeting around 21-23% of EBITDA margin for the year. Are we still online for that for the whole year? Dharmendra Jain; Yeah.

items.quote: Huber is the only company there in UK who are doing screens as a business in a very mass level. So, to enter into framework agreements and other things, yes, Mahr is one of the biggest marketing brands, which we will introduce in UK and so do in US.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of INR300-400 crore for FY25
items.quote: INR300 crores to INR400 crores today I'm telling you I will achieve it.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR1,000 crore for FY26
items.quote: INR1,000 crores next year.

items.quote: Sir, we have this -- Samruddhi is going on. And other than that, absolutely, there is no other order as of now, which is pending, unexecuted. Expected by month end, we have something in pipeline, 4, 5 more orders.

items.statement: Fundraise planned after March for FY26 growth
items.quote: We will do it after March. We are extremely busy. We have to meet our -- not only financial targets, but our physical targets are also there because in last week of May, all the construction work stops because of rains.

items.statement: Expecting INR25-30 crore rental revenue in Q4 FY25
items.quote: We are expecting about INR25 crores to INR30 crores from rentals in financial year end.

items.quote: We have one small problem. We have billing with government and they are really slow, what to do.

items.quote: So that is why for clarity, I have created three. One more will be done. So it is not only for investors, it is for the taxation authorities. Everyone is getting confused. So it is -- now it is crystal clear, this work is done in this, this work is done in this, like that. And still we are having some possibility of a defense contract. So defense will be a separate subsidiary.

items.statement: Vodafone remains part of strategy; data centers and others also in pipeline
items.quote: See, as a normal business Vodafone is part of our strategy yes because it is still there and I will not discount any customer. I am putting the capacity the Vodafone is not there, somebody else will take it.

items.statement: Starlink not a threat due to capacity limitations vs fiber
items.quote: Starlink is a satellite-based communication and there is always a capacity limitation. It is not a direct threat to any of the broadband provider for that. It is basically used where there is no

items.statement: Defense indigenization discussions with Directorate of Indigenization Indian Army and armament/missile companies for metal 3D printed spares
items.quote: We are working with Directorate of Indigenization Indian Army. We are working with some armament company or maybe missile company to provide them specific parts which will be 3D printed -- metal 3D printed.

items.statement: Smart traffic signaling project still in design stage with complications
items.quote: That is still in designing stage. It is not finalized. There are some complications. So once that is done, then only our part comes into play.

items.statement: Bid for pipeline projects submitted; expects L1 status by March
items.quote: We have done bidding for pipeline projects also, and I'm sure we will be L1, but that bid opening and things are pending. So by March, I'll be able to give you some good news.

items.statement: Targets Rs 250 crore revenue and 10% PAT margin for FY25
items.quote: We are very confident that we will continue to do well on the organic growth front, expanding geographically and assuring all our investors that we are confident of achieving Rs. 250 crore revenues for the current year with a 10% PAT margin in FY25.

items.statement: Aims for Rs 100 crore PAT in next 3 financial years via organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: We are on our journey of reaching around Rs.100 crores in profit after tax in the next 3 financial years through both organic and inorganic growth.

items.statement: Internal EBITDA target range 12-15% and PAT target range 8-12%
items.quote: But at this moment, if you look at our EBITDA ranging between 12% to 15% and PAT is what in internal guidelines we have, we should have between 8% to 12% range.

items.statement: Expects increased US spending under new administration to benefit advertising and platform business
items.quote: Given the economic policies of the newly elected US administration and their "Make the Country Great" campaign, we anticipate increased spending and economic expansion, which aligns well with our business strategy.

items.statement: Digital advertising share growing at expense of print and TV; DOOH and CTV adoption rising rapidly
items.quote: The allocation of advertising spends towards digital and programmatic advertising for awareness, lead generation and conversions are increasing in the overall pie of the advertising and growing at the expens e of print and television

items.statement: 2.2 million domains under portfolio growing at 8-10% CAGR; India's second largest domain registrar
items.quote: So, in the domain business, we currently have around 2.2 million domains under our portfolio, and we are just helping and growing at roughly 8% to 10% CAGR in that particular domain side.

items.statement: Investing in people, geographical expansions and recruitment for growth journey
items.quote: We will make the investments required for achieving this growth, and we have already recruited the right team for this

items.statement: Opened branch in Pune; setting up footprint in UK for Europe and HK for Southeast Asia and China
items.quote: Expanded our geographic footprint by opening a branch in Pune, expecting the Company's revenue to grow at 30% for Financial Year '25 and '26.

items.statement: Works with top agencies including WPP Group, Dentsu Group, Madison and other publishers
items.quote: when you talk about the agencies in India, we work really closely with WPP Group, Den tsu Group, many other publishers, Madison, and all top agencies

items.statement: Views other AdTech companies as complementing each other rather than competing due to expanding market pie
items.quote: So, I believe that instead of competition we have to see that as a complement to each other and grow further on that.

items.statement: Actively evaluating North American acquisition targets; some LOIs received; will announce after due diligence
items.quote: We have a few North American companies as a part of a target list, and we are very closely working with them. And a few of the places we also got an LOI and we are just talking, working towards on how good they could fit with us.

items.statement: Rs 100 crore PAT target in 3 years to be achieved through combination of organic and inorganic growth
items.quote: So, we are hoping to get few inorganic as well as part of it. So, this will be combination of organic and inorganic both.

items.statement: MadTech contributes 70-80% and CloudTech 20-30% of revenue
items.quote: So, I just mentioned a few minutes back, it's around 70% to 80% on the MadTech side and 20% to 30% roughly on the CloudTech side.

items.statement: International revenue 80%, domestic 20%
items.quote: 80% of business is international while 20% of business is domestic.

items.statement: India digital media market grew from Rs 50,000 crore to Rs 69,000-70,000 crore (19% CAGR)
items.quote: India itself is roughly a 50,000-crore market of dig ital media last year, and this year is going to be around 69,000 to 70,000 crores

items.statement: Global MadTech market growing at 19.8%, CloudTech at 14.1%, domain industry at 8%
items.quote: The AdTech market is globally growing at 13.7%, whereas the MadTech market is growing even faster at 19.8%. Besides, cloud computing is growing at 14.1%, whereas the domain industry is growing at 8%.

items.statement: No dividend payout currently; focus on deploying reserves for growth; board will decide future payouts
items.quote: At this point our focus is to grow further internally, whichever way we can grow. That is the reason we have not yet started. But yes, as soon as the board decides and anything comes up on that, we will definitely start working towards what your requirement is.

items.statement: Stock price decline attributed to macro market sentiments; no promoter selling or fundamental concern
items.quote: See, basically, I mean industry has its own secondary market and its own way of behaving towards the various regions across the globe. So, we are not sure, I mean, I am a right person to comment on the secondary market side but on the Company's side, we can definitely say that your Company is good growing, and we are working very hard to grow it further faster.

items.statement: Demerger expected to be effective 1st April if NCLT order received in February
items.quote: We expect that within February we will get the order and by next financial, 1st April, the demerger will be effective.

items.statement: Distribution business targeting breakeven in FY26
items.quote: So, we will try to increase the sales and also reduce some costs so that in FY '26 the distribution business is breakeven.

items.statement: Athleisure expected to contribute 1-2% of total sales in FY26
items.quote: And we expect that in this year the sales would be around 1% or 2% of the total sales.

items.statement: Expect FY26 to be better than FY25 with volume growth and cost reduction
items.quote: We expect that FY '26 will be better compared to FY '25.

items.statement: December saw 15% growth year-on-year; wedding season Jan-Jun and Eid in March expected to boost demand
items.quote: December, from last year, we have done around 15% growth for the December month.

items.statement: Wedding season from January to June and Eid in March will increase demand in FY26
items.quote: But this year we have seen that the wedding season is there from January to June, so that will obviously increase the demand. And also, Eid in March, so this will have a good impact for the demand thing.

items.statement: Q3 gross margin declined 110 bps YoY to 44.6% due to early EOSS and higher discounting
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter stood at 44.6%, down by 110 basis point s as compared to the same period last

items.statement: 9M gross margin at 46.7%; discounting impact estimated at 2-2.5% of the 4% margin drop
items.quote: Out of the 4% around 2% to 2.5% would be for discount because this year also we have given discount in August and July also because that time it was a dry season, so we started the EOSS early.

items.statement: COCO EBITDA margin around 22-25%; overall retail EBITDA margin 16.5% for 9M
items.quote: COCO EBITDA margin is around 22% to 25%.

items.statement: Retail store count reached 890 with 61 new openings in 9M; 222 COCO and 668 franchise stores
items.quote: As of nine months FY '25, our total retail store count reached 890 with 61 new store openings during the period. Breaking this down by model, our C OO store count stood at 222 stores, while our franchise network expanded to 668 stores.

items.statement: Onboarded 50 new distributors in Q3, total 776 distributors as of 9M FY25
items.quote: Additionally, we onboarded 50 new distributors during the quarter, bringing the total to 776 as of 9 months FY '25.

items.statement: Discount sales increased from 20-22% to 30-32% of total sales due to price bracket transition
items.quote: But here what we have seen that the discount percent has increased to 30% to 32% because the flow of discounted item is comparably higher than what was there in the last financial year.

items.statement: Launching athleisure segment in Spring Summer '25 with 20 SKUs targeting eastern and southern India
items.quote: We will be introducing product with MRP of ₹ 500 to ₹ 750. In the first instance, we will be giving it to 50 stores in eastern part of the country and the southern part of the country.

items.statement: Focusing on trending products like clogs; eliminating underperforming SKUs like old chappals
items.quote: Like clogs is doing well, we are going to push more of clogs. And say like some old type of chappals are not doing well, we will try to take that out.

items.statement: Online channel contributes 4-5% of sales; focusing on selective product basket and online marketing
items.quote: So, the percentage of online business, I mean, it's somewhere around 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Converting 30-odd underperforming franchise stores to commission-based model to boost sales
items.quote: So that way we have done a few stores, around 30-odd stores. And we are seeing a good response from that.

items.statement: Quick commerce partnership with Zepto on hold until warehouse shift to Ekart completes
items.quote: So, once it starts, we will start the Zepto thing. A ll the agreements and everything has been done , s o once the place is finalized and operative, then we will start that

items.statement: Outsourcing e-commerce warehousing to Ekart to convert fixed cost to variable cost
items.quote: Mainly we are converting the fixed cost into variable cost actually.

items.statement: Distribution PBT loss not tracked separately due to combined finance cost and depreciation
items.quote: PBT level we do not track, because of the finance cost and the depreciation are a combined thing.

items.statement: Demerger pending NCLT final hearing; order expected in February with reserve date 21st February
items.quote: Demerger is pending before the NCL T for the final orders . So, the dates are, I think within February we will get, the dates will be on 21st February

items.statement: Retail volume grew from 17.49 lakh to 17.96 lakh pairs in Q3; 9M retail volume 54 lakh pairs, distribution 1.70 crore pairs
items.quote: In the third quarter, we have seen that t he volume of the retail business from 17,49,000 pair has gone up to 17,96,000 pair

items.statement: Same store sales growth flat for last 2-3 years; price reduction aimed at improving SSG
items.quote: At present at same store there is no growth, we are having the problem of same store growth. We have seen the last two, three years there's no growth in same store.

items.statement: COCO store annual sales range ₹1.5 cr to ₹24-25 cr per month; franchise secondary sales ₹18-20 cr per month
items.quote: We have COCO having average sales of around ₹ 24 crores to ₹ 25 crores in a month.

items.statement: Distribution ASP ₹96; Retail ASP ₹539
items.quote: In distribution it is 96 and in retail it is 539.

items.statement: Macro conditions not good; inflationary cost pressure impacting profitability
items.quote: The current market condition is not good, the macro condition is not good, but still, we are trying to increase the sale through various modes.

items.statement: Soda ash EBITDA target 18-20% at current prices after machinery installation
items.quote: We would. at a full steady state as our internal assumption goals would do an EBITDA of 18%-20% at current prices.

items.statement: Legacy term debt to be repaid in 2-2.5 years; new CPVC capex debt has 5-year tenure
items.quote: I think in 2 to 2.5 years' time, we will be able to pay off the legacy debt. The debt, which has been recently taken to support the CPVC CAPEX will have a 5-year window.

items.statement: CPVC Phase-3 first phase (20K to 40K TPA) volumes to be placed gradually from Q3 FY26
items.quote: We are hopeful that from Quarter 3 of next fiscal, we will be gradually placing the volumes.

items.statement: Renewable power project expected annual savings Rs 35-40 crore at current blended power prices
items.quote: I think now we anticipate the savings with the current blended prices of power to be at around Rs. 35-Rs. 40 crores.

items.statement: Synthetic rutile business to be much better in FY26 with orders booked to current production capacity at better prices
items.quote: We have been able to book orders more or less to the extent of our current production and the prices are much better than what we were able to achieve during the year 24-25.

items.statement: Alternative energy project Phase 1 operational by end of January, Phase 2 by end of March
items.quote: Our alternative energy project is near completion with the first phase expected to be operational by the end of this month and second phase by the end of March.

items.statement: CPVC expansion Phase 1 (20K to 40K TPA) construction underway, commissioning targeted by September 2025
items.quote: Our CPVC expansion project, which we announced in our previous earnings call, is progressing well. Construction is underway and we remain committed to commission the first phase by September of this year.

items.statement: SIOP debottlenecking capex approximately Rs 30-35 crore within the Rs 125 crore previous capex
items.quote: If I have to put a number on it, it would be around Rs. 30-Rs. 35 odd crore, but that specific we cannot give it to you because there are certain inter-linkage utilities which we had also built in that CAPEX.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization above 80% across all product categories in Q3; PVC and CPVC at full capacity
items.quote: For Quarter 3, we achieved overall capacity utilization above 80% across all our product categories. This is a testament to our strong operational execution and market positioning.

items.statement: Soda ash operating at 80-85% capacity for last 9 months; full 100% production expected from end of Q1 FY26
items.quote: have been presently operating at around 80 %-85% capacity for the last 9 months and we will continue to do so for Quarter 4 as well. We would have our machinery in place to support 100% production and sale going forward from end of Quarter 1

items.quote: The swing was in the commodity segment, which clocked a Rs. 14.2 crores profit as against the loss of Rs. 6 crores in the last quarter. This was again driven by the caustic prices increase by 11% and a better VC and PVC spread.

items.statement: Synthetic rutile historic margins north of 20%; recovery gradual with long-term contracts secured
items.quote: Synthetic rutile historic margins have been in the north of 20%. So there has been some demand disruption in the last year and the year under review, which has led to a decrease in our overall profitability, but this is a one-off operation.

items.statement: SIOP and CPVC EBITDA margin target 30-35% but difficult to guarantee given geopolitics
items.quote: We are hopeful that we will be able to maintain the margin of 30%-35% both in SIOP and our CPVC segment.

items.statement: CPVC realization currently around Rs 130/kg; prices move in tandem with PVC with a lag
items.quote: CPVC realization is around Rs. 130.

items.statement: Caustic soda realizations improved 12% YoY and 11% QoQ in Q3
items.quote: The major savings on the commodity EBITDA was from PVC due to positive VC and PVC spread and also from the caustic where the realizations improved by 12% in Quarter 3.

items.statement: Chinese imports causing pricing distress across chemical segments; China stimulus may ease export pressure over time

items.statement: Construction sector weakness impacting PVC/CPVC demand; availability will eventually drive demand growth
items.quote: There has been a decline in the PVC, CPVC demand in the construction sector, which has had some impact on the demand. But having said that, it is not that the prices you drop the price and you will sell.

items.statement: SIOP India market 20-25K TPA, DCW sells 9-10K TPA; major sales in US market with steady long-term commitments
items.quote: SIOP, the local demand is in the vicinity of about 20,000-25,000 tons a year out of which we are selling almost 9000 tons to 10,000 tons. Our major sales are in the US market, which is a very good and steady market for us.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals achieved highest ever sales in first 9 months of FY25; 42% EBITDA growth YoY
items.quote: Specialty chemicals, which continue to be the backbone of our growth strategy remained stable and provided the much needed margin consistency. This segment achieved its highest ever sales during the first 9 months of this fiscal.

items.statement: Synthetic rutile export sales 8 KT in Q3; orders booked to current production capacity for FY26
items.quote: The other factors were export sales of synthetic rutile, which finally saw some uptick and we could conclude our sales of above 8 KT for the quarter.

items.statement: Term lending reduced to ~Rs 395 crore from Rs 410 crore in March 2024 despite Rs 80 crore fresh borrowing for CPVC capex
items.quote: Term lending has been reducing and has reached a level of Rs. 400 crores, reduction of Rs. 410 crores in March 24 despite Rs. 80 crores of fresh borrowings to support the ongoing CPVC CAPEX.

items.statement: Weighted average cost of term lending 9.5%; interest cost declining 10% YoY and 12% QoQ
items.quote: Cost of borrowing, weighted average cost of all term lending put together will be 9.5%.

items.statement: DSO 30-40 days, creditors 90-100 days; inventory days stable QoQ, expected to decline from FY26
items.quote: Our DSO, debtors outstanding is roughly 30-40 days at the organization level. Our creditors around 90-100 days, our inventory was going up in terms of days because of the export volumes we were unable to place for synthetic rutile predominantly.

items.statement: Maintaining 5% of revenue in cash (FDs) as working capital discipline; non-fund based LCs for VCM purchases
items.quote: On the working capital side, we have followed a discipline of maintaining 5% of revenue in cash ( FDs) what we have and we are following th at discipline quite comfortably

items.statement: Provisional anti-dumping duty on PVC recommended by Commerce Ministry in October; Finance Ministry implementation pending
items.quote: On the policy front, while provisional anti-dumping duty on PVC was recommended by the Ministry of Commerce in October, its implementation by the Ministry of Finance remains pending.

items.statement: Soda ash industry liaising with government for pricing support; MIP (minimum import price) also being pursued
items.quote: Industry has also been talking with the government in terms of pricing supports, and there has been MIP which is also coming on the minimum imports into the country.

items.statement: 40-45% of SIOP production exported to US; no specific Trump tariffs on India yet; 10% China tariff may help

And we want to now hit INR 50 crores odd, which will be INR 600 crores odd. And then we talk of INR 80 crores, which will be basically INR 1,000 crores odd a year.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 gross margin expanded 279 bps YoY to 56.2% driven by better product mix and lower raw material prices
items.quote: Gross margin expanded by 279 basis points from 53.5% to 56.2% in Q3 FY25. This was driven by a better product mix and lower raw material prices.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin declined 234 bps YoY to 20.4% due to new facility employee costs and higher freight
items.quote: The reduction in EBITDA margin by 234 basis points was primarily due to the addition of new employees at the Teva facility and increase in freight costs.

items.statement: Freight cost headwind easing; expect no drag on EBITDA from Q4 FY25; employee cost drag to ease in 1-2 quarters as revenue grows
items.quote: I think that impact you should see in this quarter, in Q4. I think this will no longer be a drag on EBITDA from this quarter onwards. And the employee cost also, I think as revenue grows, it will be again no drag on EBITDA from next 1 or 2 quarters.

items.statement: Sustainable gross margin level around 56% (Q3 level) going forward; Q2 59% was unsustainable
items.quote: So, I think those margins are now becoming more at a level that will be more sustainable.

items.statement: U.S. revenue grew 37% YoY to INR 353 crores in Q3 FY25 driven by new product launches and market share gains

items.statement: U.K. & EU revenue grew 2.6% YoY to INR 258 crores in Q3 FY25; softness attributed to warm winter seasonality

items.statement: Raw material costs stable and softened; no expected increase currently

items.statement: Abhilaya FY26 revenue target of Rs 117-120 crores with breakeven expected
items.quote: And hopefully, curtai ling down these 3PL logistics and additional business from Amazon, next financial year definitely we will be breaking even, and anticipating a top line of close to ₹117 crores to ₹120 crores will be achievable.

items.statement: Abhilaya FY27 revenue target of over Rs 200 crores contingent on funding
items.quote: So, hopefully, once that gets done, the top line, if we can plan provided we get a fund, then we can really achieve more than ₹200 crores turnover by next financial year.

items.statement: Abhilaya sustainable EBITDA margin target of 4-5%
items.quote: See, the EBITDA margin will be around close to 4% -5% on that basis.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA margin improved to 3.9%, up 143 bps YoY and 176 bps QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% expanding 143 basis points YoY and 176 basis points on QoQ, reflecting better cost management and cost control measures that we have taken for these nine -month periods.

items.statement: Higher container density (58 to 61+ CBM) driving EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: The containers what we are stuffing it, earlier used close to 58 cubic meters in the 40 feet container, which we will be now achieving more than 61 cubic meters. So higher density, which is an improvisation of our productivity is helping us to achieve more higher EBITDA margin.

items.statement: LCL export volume robust at 67,767 CBMs in Q3 FY25
items.quote: In LCL consolidation, export volume remained robust at 67,767 CBMs, ensuring stability in the overall global trade flows.

items.statement: FCL export volume grew 9% QoQ to 3,782 TEUs in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Full load containers freight forwarding saw a 9% QoQ increase in exports, rising from 3,485 TEUs in Q2 FY25 to 3,782 TEUs in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Air cargo export volume surged 52% QoQ to 414 tonnes in Q3 FY25
items.quote: The air cargo freight segment witnessed remarkable growth with export volumes surging 52%, QoQ from 272 tons in Q2 FY25 to 414 tonnes in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Abhilaya focusing on vendor business with Amazon, Flipkart and partnering for Amazon quick commerce from April
items.quote: We are focusing only mainly on our vendor business which is Amazon, Flipkart, and other small e-commerce operator companies. And we will be participating with Amazon for their quick commerce deliveries which they are coming up from April onwards.

items.statement: Flipkart Diwali shipments exceeded 4.5 million in a month
items.quote: Because Diwali was quite good, we achieved more than 4.5 million shipments in that particular month itself, which is again pushing us to give us some profitability also.

items.statement: Container shipping rates fell 10% in last three months and 50% from July 2024 highs
items.quote: Also, in the container shipping market, we continue to experience price declines with rate s falling 10% in the last three months and nearly 50% from their July 2024 highs, reflecting easing supply chain bottlenecks, allowing for greater cost efficiency in ocean transport.

items.statement: Aviation turbine fuel prices stable in January 2025, down 23% from October 2023 peak
items.quote: Additionally, aviation turbine fuel prices remained stable in January 2025, down 23% from the ir peak in October'23, helping manage air freight operational expenses.

items.statement: GST e-way bill volumes grew 5.5% MoM in January 2025, strongest since October 2023
items.quote: GST e-way bill volumes saw a 5.5% month-on-month increase in January 2025, marking the strongest growth since October'23.

items.statement: Port volumes up 6% YoY, container volumes up 15% YoY
items.quote: Port operations remained robust, with overall volumes increased by 6% year-on-year, while container volume surged 15% year-on-year, likely influenced by business exp editing shipments ahead of anticipated higher US tariffs.

items.statement: Seeking private equity or other funding to expand Abhilaya dark stores across multiple cities
items.quote: So, this is our plan and we are looking for some fund arrangements from either so me private equity funds as well as through other sources also.

items.statement: Curtailing 3PL logistics and dark store expansion to focus on vendor business and Amazon quick commerce
items.quote: So, we are curtailing down these 3PL efforts for some time because this requires a lot of, again, the funding arrangements for this. We have to expand in various locations. So, we are focusing only mainly on our vendor business which is Amazon, Flipkart, and other small e-commerce operator companies.

items.statement: Expanding FCL business across pan-India offices in Gujarat, West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, South India
items.quote: The strategies, we are more focusing on the full load containers business at various locations where we have offices on pan-India level, more from the Gujarat side, more from the Calcutta side, I mean, West Bengal side, more from Tamil Nadu and the South I ndia side.

items.statement: Dark store expansion requires funding and burning for at least a year before breakeven
items.quote: Because this really gives us some revenue but it requires funding and burning for at lea st a year. And second financial year onwards we can do the breakeven and third we can start making money.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 revenue Rs 145 crores, up 63.9% YoY; 9M FY25 revenue Rs 427 crores, up 56.5% YoY
items.quote: Revenues for the quarter stood at ₹145 crores, reflecting 63.9% YoY growth compared to Q3 FY24. For 9M FY25, revenue reached ₹427 crores, marking a 56.5% YoY increase.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 EBITDA Rs 5.7 crores, up 2.6x YoY; 9M FY25 EBITDA Rs 11.9 crores, up 58.7% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for Q3 FY25 grew to ₹5.7 crores, a 2.6x increase YoY, indicating higher operational efficiency. EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% expanding 143 basis points YoY and 176 basis points on QoQ, reflecting better cost management and cost control measures that we have taken for these nine -month periods , EBITDA has reached ₹11.9 crores, which is a 58.7% increase YoY.

items.statement: Q3 FY25 PAT Rs 3.3 crores, up 2x YoY; 9M FY25 PAT Rs 7.6 crores, up 44.6% YoY
items.quote: During Q3 FY25, profit after tax has increased to ₹3.3 crores, reflecting 2x YoY growth, while PAT for the nine months stood at ₹7.6 crores, a 44.6% YoY increase.
